title: 小星星的暖暖
preview: 在一个很远很远的地方，有一片安静的山谷。山谷里有一条浅浅的小溪，溪水叮叮咚咚，像在唱一首永远唱不完的歌...
moral: 被爱是一种温暖，爱别人是一种力量。这世界上的每一份在乎，都是一束看不见却永远不会熄灭的光。愿你被爱包围，也愿你成为别人的光。
content: 在一个很远很远的地方，有一片安静的山谷。山谷里有一条浅浅的小溪，溪水叮叮咚咚，像在唱一首永远唱不完的歌。
小溪边住着一只小兔子，名字叫棉棉。棉棉有一身像云朵一样柔软的白毛，和一双总是亮晶晶的大眼睛。
每天晚上，棉棉都会坐在溪边的大石头上，看着天上一颗一颗亮起来的星星。她最喜欢的是最亮的那一颗——那颗星星叫「暖暖」。
「暖暖，暖暖，」棉棉轻轻地说，「你离我那么远，会不会孤单呀？」
这天晚上，棉棉刚说完，就看见溪水里映着的星星忽然闪了一下。然后，一个小小的光点从水面上飘了起来，亮闪闪的，像一颗迷你的小太阳。
「你好呀，棉棉。」光点发出温柔的声音。
「你……你是暖暖吗？」棉棉惊讶地问。
「是呀。我听见你每天晚上都在跟我说话。」暖暖的光一闪一闪的，「我一点也不孤单，因为我知道你在看着我。被人在乎的感觉，就是最温暖的陪伴呀。」
棉棉开心极了，她和暖暖聊了很多很多：聊山谷里的花什么时候开，聊小溪里的小鱼爱玩什么游戏，聊风吹过树林时树叶会唱什么歌。
暖暖说：「棉棉，你知道吗？世界上有一种光，比星星更亮。」
「是什么光？」棉棉好奇地竖起耳朵。
「是爱呀。」暖暖轻轻地说，「当一个生命被另一个生命深深地爱着的时候，那种光比所有的星星加起来还要亮。你看不见它，但它一直都在。就像你每天来看我，就像风每天拥抱山谷，就像小溪永远陪着石头。」
棉棉听得入了神。她想起妈妈每天给她准备的胡萝卜，想起爸爸驮着她跳过小溪去看花，想起朋友们在草地上一起打滚儿的下午。
「原来我一直被这么多光包围着呀。」棉棉的心里暖暖的。
「是呀，」暖暖说，「而且将来，还会有更多更多的光来到你身边。也许是一个新朋友，也许是一个你想保护的人，也许是一个小小的、软软的、需要你牵着的手。」
棉棉的眼睛更亮了：「我会好好爱每一个来到我身边的人。」
暖暖慢慢地飘起来，越飘越高，回到了天上的星星群里。不过这一次，棉棉觉得天上的每一颗星星，都在对她眨眼睛，都变成了「暖暖」。
山谷里安安静静的。小溪还在叮叮咚咚地唱歌。棉棉趴在石头上，慢慢地闭上了眼睛，嘴角挂着甜甜的笑。
她知道，明天天亮的时候，山谷还在，小溪还在，爱她的和她爱的人，都在。
而那些看不见的光，也会一直在——在每一阵风里，在每一片叶子里，在每一个温柔的晚安里。
晚安，棉棉。
晚安，每一个被爱包围的小生命。

title: 小种子的春天
preview: 在春天刚刚到来的时候，一颗小小的种子落在了柔软湿润的泥土里。她圆圆滚滚的，裹着一层浅褐色的外衣，安安静静地睡着了...
moral: 世界上最深的爱，是在你还没有到来之前，就已经开始了。有一个人在等你，用尽了所有的温柔与耐心。愿你带着这份爱，勇敢地来到这个世界——因为你，本身就是最美的花开。
content: 在春天刚刚到来的时候，一颗小小的种子落在了柔软湿润的泥土里。她圆圆滚滚的，裹着一层浅褐色的外衣，安安静静地睡着了。
泥土里很黑，也很安静。可是小种子一点也不害怕，因为她能感觉到，头顶上有一片暖暖的东西，像一床看不见的被子，轻轻地盖着她。后来她才知道，那叫做「阳光」。
有一天，小种子在梦里听见了一个声音。那声音软软的、甜甜的，像是滴在花瓣上的露水。
「你好呀，小宝贝。」那个声音轻轻地说。
小种子动了动，她想回答，却发现自己还不会说话。她只能轻轻地晃了晃自己的壳。
那个声音又来了，每天都会来。有时候是早晨，声音里带着鸟鸣一样的清脆；有时候是傍晚，声音里带着晚风一样的温柔。声音的主人会给她唱歌，会给她讲泥土外面的世界——讲蓝得像宝石一样的天空，讲白得像棉花糖一样的云朵，讲那些飞来飞去、唱着歌的小鸟。
「等你出来了，我带你看最好看的花，喝最甜的露水，在草地上打一个下午的滚儿。」声音这样对她说。
小种子虽然听不懂全部，但她觉得心里暖洋洋的。她开始用力地吸收土壤里的养分，让自己的身体一天比一天饱满。她想快一点长大，她想看看那个每天对她说话的人，是什么样子的。
春雨来了，细细密密的雨丝渗进泥土里，像无数双温柔的手，轻轻托着她。春风也来了，在泥土外面呼呼地吹着，像在喊：「加油呀，加油呀，我们在外面等你！」
小种子越来越有力气了。她伸了伸身体，发现自己长出了一条白白嫩嫩的小尾巴——那是她的根，正牢牢地抓住脚下的泥土。她又往上挺了挺，头顶上冒出了一点嫩绿色的小芽。
「我快要看见你了。」小种子在心里默默地说。
终于有一天，小种子——不，现在她已经是一棵小苗了——用尽了全身的力气，向上一顶。
她破土而出了。
第一缕阳光轻轻地落在她的两片小叶子上。暖洋洋的。她眨了眨眼睛——如果叶子也能眨眼睛的话——看见了这个世界。
世界好大，好亮，好美。天空果然像蓝宝石，云朵果然像棉花糖，远处果然有小鸟在唱歌。
然后，她看到了那个每天对她说话的人。
那是一位年轻的妈妈。她蹲在小苗面前，眼里满是亮晶晶的东西——后来小苗知道，那叫「眼泪」，是开心的眼泪。妈妈的嘴角弯成了月牙，她的手轻轻地、小心翼翼地碰了碰小苗的叶子，像碰一颗世界上最珍贵的宝石。
「你终于来了。」妈妈轻轻地说，「我等你，等了整整一个春天。」
小苗迎着风摇了摇叶子。她想说好多好多话，可是她还是一棵小苗，还不会说话。
不过没关系。在未来的日子里，她有的是时间。她会开出最美的花给妈妈看，会在风里跳舞给妈妈看，会用每一片叶子、每一朵花瓣，告诉妈妈——
「谢谢你，在我还只是泥土里一颗小小的种子的时候，就已经那么那么地爱我。」

title: 小星星的礼物
preview: 在蓝蓝的天空尽头，住着一颗小小的星星。她没有别的星星那么大，也没有别的星星那么亮，但她有一颗特别温柔的心...
moral: 你还没来到这个世界的时候，就已经有人在默默地爱你、守护你了。你本身就是一份珍贵无比的礼物，带着满满的星光与期待。愿你带着这份温柔的爱，安心地成长——世界在等你，星星也在等你。
content: 在蓝蓝的天空尽头，住着一颗小小的星星。她没有别的星星那么大，也没有别的星星那么亮，但她有一颗特别温柔的心。每天晚上，她都会眨着亮晶晶的眼睛，安安静静地守着夜空。
有一天，小星星低头往下望，她看见一间温暖的小房子。窗户里透出橘黄色的灯光，一位妈妈正坐在床边，轻轻地拍着一个圆滚滚的小肚子，嘴里哼着一首好听的曲子。
小星星听啊听，她觉得那首曲子比天上的任何声音都好听。她好想送给这位妈妈和这个还没出生的小宝宝一份礼物。
可是星星能送什么礼物呢？她没有双手，不能包礼物；她没有口袋，不能装糖果。小星星有点发愁。
她跑去问月亮婆婆。月亮婆婆弯着银白色的眉毛，笑眯眯地说：「小傻瓜，你本身就是礼物呀。你的光，就是这世上最温柔的守护。」
小星星歪着脑袋想了想，她决定要做一件特别的事情。
从那天起，每当那位妈妈哄小宝宝睡觉的时候，小星星就把自己调到最亮、最温柔的模式。她不像流星那样急匆匆地划过，也不像烟花那样噼里啪啦地炸开——她只是安安静静地，在窗外的那一小片天空里，一闪，一闪，像一颗挂在天上的小夜灯。
她还请来了风姐姐。风姐姐轻轻地、轻轻地，从窗户缝里溜进去，把院子里的茉莉花香带进了房间。那香味淡淡的，像妈妈在宝宝额头上落下的吻。
她还请来了蟋蟀弟弟。蟋蟀弟弟在窗台下的草丛里，拉起了他的小提琴——「蛐蛐，蛐蛐，蛐——」声音轻轻的，软软的，像一首专门为小宝宝写的催眠曲。
有一天晚上，月亮婆婆特别高兴，她在天上铺开了一条银色的小路，从星星的家一直铺到那扇小窗户。小星星沿着这条小路，慢慢地滑下来——当然，她不会真的掉下来，她只是把自己暖暖的光，顺着月光一起，轻轻地洒进了房间。
小宝宝虽然还在妈妈的肚子里，但好像什么都感觉到了。他在水里翻了个小小的跟头，把妈妈的肚皮顶起了一个圆圆的小包。
妈妈低下头，温柔地摸了摸那个小包，笑着说：「你是不是也看见窗外的那颗小星星啦？她每天晚上都来陪我们呢。」
小星星在天上听见了，高兴得整颗心都亮了起来。她知道了，原来礼物不需要很大，不需要很贵重。一颗愿意陪伴的心，一束愿意守护的光，就是最好的礼物。
后来，小宝宝出生了。那是个有着亮晶晶眼睛的小婴儿。妈妈给他取了一个名字，叫做「小辰」。因为「辰」就是星星的意思。
每天晚上，当妈妈哄小辰睡觉的时候，她都会指着窗外的那颗小星星，轻轻地说：「看，那是你的守护星。她在你还没出生的时候，就开始爱你了。」
而小星星呢，她依然每天晚上都守在那扇窗户外面，一闪，一闪，用最温柔的光，守护着这个她用尽全心去爱的孩子。
因为她知道——爱，是世界上唯一不会熄灭的星光。

title: 雨滴在云里等（胎教期）
preview: 云妈妈的口袋里，住着一滴小小的雨。她圆圆的，透明的，还没去过地面，也没闻过泥土的味道...
moral: 等待不是空的。等待里装着所有的期盼、所有的温柔、所有还没说出口的爱。当你终于来到这个世界，你会发现——你等的人，也在等你。
content: 云妈妈的口袋里，住着一滴小小的雨。她圆圆的，透明的，还没去过地面，也没闻过泥土的味道。
小雨滴每天趴在云的边沿上，往下看。她看见田野、河流、小房子。其中一栋小房子的窗户亮着橘黄色的灯，灯里有一位妈妈，正轻轻地拍着圆圆的肚子，嘴里哼着歌。
小雨滴想下去。她想去看看那扇亮着灯的窗户。听说那肚子里住着一个还没来的小宝宝，跟小雨滴一样，也在等。
云妈妈说：「再等等。雨要落下去，得等风准备好了，得等土地渴了，得等太阳把云晒得暖暖的、软软的。」
小雨滴等啊等。她听云妈妈讲地面的故事——讲小草怎么从泥土里钻出来，讲小溪怎么在石头之间弹钢琴，讲花儿怎么在风里点头。
「地面是什么感觉？」小雨滴问。
「地面是温暖的。」云妈妈说，「像一双一直在等你的手。」
有一天，风来了。风从很远的地方来，带着田野的味道，带着花香，还带着一个声音——一个妈妈在轻轻哼歌的声音。
小雨滴听见了那首歌。她觉得那首歌是在叫她。也许不是叫她，但那首歌的旋律刚好跟她心里的节拍一模一样。
云妈妈把口袋松了一点点。小雨滴滑到了口袋的边沿上。
「准备好了吗？」云妈妈问。
「准备好了。」小雨滴说。她不怕。因为她知道，下面有人在等——妈妈在等宝宝，土地在等雨，而她，正要去赴一场温暖的相遇。
小雨滴落了下去。风轻轻地托着她，不急，不慌。她穿过云层，穿过风，穿过鸟的翅膀旁边，穿过树叶的缝隙。
她落在了一片叶子上，嗒。又从叶子上滑到了泥土里，渗进去了。
泥土很黑，但很温暖。小雨滴觉得自己被什么柔软的东西包裹住了，像被一双手轻轻捧着。
泥土里，有一颗种子，也在等。种子感觉到雨来了，动了一下，好像在说：「你来了。」
小雨滴和种子，在泥土里相遇了。一个从天上来的，一个在地里等的。它们谁也没说话，但都觉得——原来等了这么久，就是为了这一刻。
窗户里，妈妈的歌还在轻轻地响。她不知道，她的歌叫来了一滴雨，而雨叫醒了一颗种子。
每一个等待，都在等一个相遇。而每一个相遇，都让等待变得值得。

title: The Pond Sleeps Too (Prenatal)
preview: The pond goes shhh-shhh when the sun goes down. The cattails go swish-swish at the edge. The old willow goes sway-sway over the water...
moral: When everything around you breathes slow and soft, you can breathe slow and soft too. The pond knows how to sleep. The moon knows how to wait. And you - you know how to be still, even if you don't know it yet.
content: The pond goes shhh-shhh when the sun goes down.
The cattails go swish-swish at the edge. The old willow goes sway-sway over the water.
A small duck, name of Pip, floats on the pond. Pip is brown. Pip is small. Pip is doing nothing. Just floating.
The bullfrog says: rummm... rummm... rummm... from the mud. Low and slow and round, like a belly full of warm soup.
The fireflies come out. Blink... blink... blink... Like tiny lanterns that someone forgot to blow out.
Mama Duck paddles over. Paddle, paddle, paddle. She settles next to Pip. She doesn't say anything. She just settles. The water barely moves.
The moon comes up. It comes up slow, slow, slow - like it's being very careful not to wake anything up.
The moon puts a silver road on the water. It goes from the edge of the pond all the way to where Pip is floating. Pip doesn't know it's there. But the road is there.
Shhh-shhh says the water. Rummm-rummm says the frog. Blink-blink say the fireflies.
A fish jumps - plop - and the ripples go round and round and round, getting bigger and softer, until they disappear into the dark.
The old willow drops a leaf. The leaf falls slow, slow, slow - side to side, side to side - and lands on the water without a sound. It floats there, like a tiny green boat.
Pip's eyes go heavy. Pip tucks his beak under his wing. Warm. Close. Mama is here.
The whole pond goes still. Not dead-still - alive-still. The kind of still that means everything is breathing together. The water, the frog, the fireflies, the duck, the moon.
Shhh... shhh... shhh...
The pond sleeps too.

title: 月光写的一封信（胎教期）
preview: 月亮给一栋小房子写了一封信。信很短，只有一句话：嘘，我在。风当邮差，把信从天上送下来...
moral: 有些爱，不需要语言，不需要文字。一束光，一阵风，一个小小的动作，就够了。你知道的——有人一直在你头顶亮着。
content: 月亮给一栋小房子写了一封信。
信很短，只有一句话：嘘，我在。
风当邮差，把信从天上送下来。风轻轻地，轻轻地，从窗户缝里溜进去。
信落在妈妈的肚子上。
妈妈没看见信，但宝宝看见了。宝宝在暖暖的羊水里，翻了个身，像在拆信。
信没有字，只有月光。月光是软的，是凉的，是一根银色的线，从天上一直牵到妈妈肚子里。
宝宝顺着这根线，往上摸了摸。他摸到了月亮。
月亮说：我每天晚上都给你写信。
宝宝不会说话，但他动了一下，像在回信。
月亮笑了。月亮的笑，就是一整片亮。
那天晚上，小房子里的灯灭了，月光没灭。
月光从窗户缝里渗进来，铺在地板上，铺在被子上，铺在妈妈的手背上。
妈妈睡得很沉。她不知道，月光在替她守着宝宝。
宝宝在月光里，安安静静地浮着。他抓着那根银色的线，线的另一头，是月亮。
月亮什么也没做。只是亮着。
但宝宝觉得很安心。
因为有些陪伴，不需要做什么。亮着，就够了。
嘘，我在。
每天晚上，月亮都会写这封信。信永远只有一句话，但那句话，比所有的故事都长。

title: The Hush-Hush Tree (Prenatal)
preview: Deep in the hush of the Whispering Wood, where the moss grows soft and the silence is good, there stood a tall tree with a curious sound - it went hush, hush, hush, all the way round...
moral: There's a hush that's not 'be quiet' - it's 'you're safe now, you can rest.' The whole world is full of that hush, if you know how to hear it. And you will.
content: Deep in the hush of the Whispering Wood, where the moss grows soft and the silence is good, there stood a tall tree with a curious sound - it went hush, hush, hush, all the way round.
Not a loud hush, not a scoldy-type hush. Not a 'be-quiet-you' hush or a 'hurry-up' hush. It was soft as a feather on fur on a rug. It was warm as a hug from a big fuzzy bug.
The Hush-Hush Tree stood with its branches spread wide, and out of its leaves came a sound soft and slow - a sound like a shush that was saying 'it's time to let go.'
Now, nobody knew where the hush-hush came from. Not the fox with his socks, not the mole with his drum, not the owl on the bough (who said 'Hoo? Hoo? Hmm?').

But a small mother bird who had built her small nest right there in the Hush-Hush Tree's branches - she knew. She had five small eggs, round and warm, and she sat on them every night from dusk until dawn.

And the hush-hush sound went shhhh... shhhh... shhhh... and the eggs didn't wiggle, and the eggs didn't squirm. They just sat in the nest, warm and still, like a handful of smooth round stones in the sun.

The mother bird sang: 'Hush little ones, hush little ones, hush. The world is still turning, but we don't need to rush. The stars are all waking, the moon's on her way. Close your small eyes - it's the end of the day.'
And the Hush-Hush Tree went shhhh... shhhh... shhhh... like it was singing along.

The wind came to visit, the way that wind does. It tickled the leaves and it made the branches buzz. But even the wind, when it passed through the tree, went 'hush' instead of 'whooo' - it couldn't help but agree.

The fireflies came, blink-blink-blink, one by one. The crickets came, chirp-chirp-chirp, under the moon. And each one of them, when they came to the tree, got quieter and quieter - as quiet as could be.

And down in the world, past the Whispering Wood, past the meadow and stream, past the houses that stood - in one of those houses, a window glowed gold. And inside the window, a mother (I'm told) was holding her belly and humming a tune, a soft little melody, under the moon.
And that melody floated right up through the air, past the chimney and rooftop, past everywhere - all the way to the Hush-Hush Tree, where it landed on a leaf like a drop of warm tea.
And the tree drank it in, and the hush got softer. And the eggs in the nest got warmer and softer. And the mother bird smiled - or as much as a bird can smile - and she whispered: 'Goodnight.'
Shhhh... shhhh... shhhh... went the Hush-Hush Tree.
And the whole wide world went as soft as could be.

title: 风知道你的名字（胎教期）
preview: 风轻轻吹，草轻轻摇，月亮轻轻走过山岗。风从山岗上跑下来，路过一棵老槐树，路过一片芦苇荡，路过一栋亮着灯的小房子...
moral: 你的名字，是这世界对你说的第一句情话。在你还没来到之前，风已经帮你传开了，水已经帮你记住了。你来了，满世界都在喊你。
content: 风轻轻吹，草轻轻摇，月亮轻轻走过山岗。
风从山岗上跑下来，路过一棵老槐树，路过一片芦苇荡，路过一栋亮着灯的小房子。
小房子的窗户开着一条缝。风从缝里溜进去，带进来桂花的香、泥土的潮，和远处小溪叮叮咚咚的声音。
妈妈坐在床边，一只手拍着圆圆的肚子，另一只手放在嘴边，好像在说什么悄悄话。
风竖起耳朵，听了听。
妈妈在说一个名字。一遍，又一遍。轻轻的，像在念一首只有两个字的诗。
风记住了那个名字。
风从窗户里出来，往田野跑。它跑过小溪，小溪叮叮咚咚，风把那个名字告诉了水。水记住了，叮叮咚咚地唱着那个名字。
风跑过老槐树，老槐树沙沙响，风把那个名字告诉了树叶。树叶记住了，沙沙沙沙地念着那个名字。
风跑过芦苇荡，芦苇轻轻摇，风把那个名字告诉了月光。月光记住了，把那个名字写在了每一片叶子的尖尖上，亮晶晶的。
风跑累了，回到小房子的屋檐上歇脚。它往下看，看见妈妈已经睡着了，手还放在肚子上。
风想，宝宝还不知道，自己的名字已经被整个世界记住了。
等宝宝来了，他会发现：溪水在叫他的名字，树叶在念他的名字，月光在写他的名字。
他一来到这个世界，就会被叫一声。那一声，全世界一起喊。
叮叮咚咚。沙沙沙沙。嘘——嘘——。
都是那个名字。
风轻轻地吹，草轻轻地摇。月亮轻轻地走过山岗，带着那个名字，走过每一扇亮着灯的窗。

title: The Old River Tells a Story (Prenatal)
preview: Well now, you listen here, and I'll tell you something about the Old Muddy that most folks don't know. The river talks. Not loud - a river doesn't need to be loud...
moral: The river has been telling stories since before there were people to listen. And it's been saving one - just for you. When you're ready, go down to the water and sit. It'll tell you. It's been waiting.
content: Well now, you listen here, and I'll tell you something about the Old Muddy that most folks don't know.
The river talks. Not loud - a river doesn't need to be loud. It talks the way an old man talks on a porch at sundown: slow, and easy, and not in any particular hurry to get to the point.

The river talks to the banks. It talks to the willows. It talks to the catfish and the turtles and the herons that stand in the shallows like they've got all the time in creation, which - being herons - they probably figure they do.
But the river's best talking? That happens at night. When the steamboats have gone and the lanterns are dim and the only ones still awake are the river and the moon.
That's when the river tells stories.

It tells about the spring floods, when it gets up over its banks and goes roaming through the bottoms like a dog that's slipped its leash. It tells about the summer doldrums, when it gets so low and slow you could walk across it and barely wet your knees. It tells about the winter ice, when it goes hard and quiet, and you can hear it groaning in the dark, like a man turning over in bed.
But there's one story the river tells that's different from the rest. It's not about floods or ice or catfish the size of dogs. It's about a sound.

'There's a sound,' the river says (or the river would say, if rivers could talk, which I'm telling you they can), 'that I've been hearing for a while now. It comes from a house on my bank. It's small - smaller than a cricket, smaller than a raindrop. But it's got a rhythm to it.'
The moon, who's been listening to the river's stories for as long as there've been rivers and moons, asks: 'What kind of rhythm?'
'A heartbeat rhythm,' the river says. 'Thump... thump... thump. Slow and steady, like a small drum in a small room.'
'Whose heartbeat?' the moon asks.

The river doesn't answer right away. It gurgles over a rock - that's river for 'let me think.' Then it says: 'There's a woman in that house who's been coming down to my bank every evening. She puts her hand on her belly and she hums. And under the hum, I can hear it - thump... thump... thump. Two heartbeats. One big, one small. The small one is new.'
The moon knows what that means. The moon has seen more new heartbeats than anybody. The moon says: 'That's a baby.'
'I know,' says the river. 'But the baby hasn't come yet. It's still in there, still growing, still thumping away. I can hear it getting stronger every week.'
'What are you going to do?' the moon asks.
The river thinks about this for a long time. Water goes over rocks. A fish jumps - plop. A frog says rummm.

'I'm going to keep talking,' the river says. 'I'm going to keep flowing past that house, nice and easy, so the baby can hear me. When it's born, it'll know my sound. It'll know the Old Muddy. And maybe - maybe - when it's old enough, it'll come down to the bank and sit, and listen, and the river will tell it stories.'
'Like what stories?' the moon asks.
'Like this one,' the river says.

And the river flowed on, under the moon, past the house with the two heartbeats, carrying its story downstream - where it would be told again, and again, and again, to every child who ever sat on a riverbank and wondered what the water was saying.

title: 小闹钟学唱歌（胎教期）
preview: 孩子们，你们知道吗？每个闹钟都会唱歌。可不是「叮铃铃」那种歌，是一种更轻、更慢的歌，是专门哄小宝宝睡觉的歌...
moral: 声音最大的不一定最有力量。最轻的声音，反而能让人放下所有的紧张，安心入睡。你的心跳也是这样——轻轻地跳，却陪了你一辈子。
content: 孩子们，你们知道吗？每个闹钟都会唱歌。
可不是「叮铃铃」那种歌，是一种更轻、更慢的歌，是专门哄小宝宝睡觉的歌。
后来啊，有一个小闹钟，住在床头柜上，它就特别想学这首歌。
小闹钟问闹钟妈妈：「妈妈妈妈，我什么时候才能学会哄觉的歌呀？」
闹钟妈妈说：「你得先学会，把自己的声音调到最小。嘀嗒嘀嗒，不能再响了，得变成嘀——嗒——嘀——嗒——，慢悠悠的。」
小闹钟试了试。嘀嗒嘀嗒嘀嗒。不行，太快了，像小兔子蹦。
它又试了试。嘀——嗒——嘀——嗒——。嗯，好一点了，像老乌龟爬。
闹钟妈妈说：「还不够。你得把声音再放轻，轻到像羽毛落在棉花上。」
小闹钟使劲儿把声音调小。嘀————嗒————。这一回，声音小得几乎听不见了。
可你猜怎么着？正因为太小了，你反而会竖起耳朵，认认真真地听。这可就对了。
闹钟妈妈笑了：「闹钟的歌，不是为了让人听见，是为了让人安静下来。」
小闹钟明白了。它开始嘀——嗒——嘀——嗒——，一声一声，不急不慌，像一只温柔的手掌，一下一下拍着后背。
床头柜旁边，妈妈哄着肚子里的宝宝。宝宝的呼吸，慢慢地跟小闹钟的嘀嗒声合拍了。
嘀——嗒——。宝宝的心跳。
嘀——嗒——。妈妈的手掌。
嘀——嗒——。小闹钟的歌。
三个声音叠在一起，变成了一首只有三拍的摇篮曲。
小闹钟可得意了。它想，原来闹钟不只是用来叫人起床的，闹钟也能哄人睡觉呀。
晚安，小闹钟。晚安，小宝宝。明天早上，小闹钟会叫你们起床的。但现在，先好好睡一觉吧。

title: The Mama Robin's Counting Song (Prenatal)
preview: In the old maple by the fence, there's a robin's nest. Mama Robin built it herself - twigs and mud and grass, pressed together with her chest, round and smooth and strong...
moral: Before you come into the world, someone is already counting you. Not days, not weeks - heartbeats. One, two, three, four. Each one a promise. Each one a 'you're almost here.'
content: In the old maple by the fence, there's a robin's nest.
Mama Robin built it herself - twigs and mud and grass, pressed together with her chest, round and smooth and strong. She built it in the fork of two branches, where the wind couldn't reach.
In the nest are four eggs. Blue as a spring sky after rain. Smooth and small and warm.
Every evening, when the sun goes down behind the barn and the fireflies come out, Mama Robin settles on the nest. She covers the eggs with her soft brown body, and she counts.
She doesn't count out loud. She counts with her heartbeat.
Thump. One egg. Thump. Two eggs. Thump. Three eggs. Thump. Four eggs.
Four heartbeats back. Four tiny thumps, so small you'd need to be a bird to feel them, pulsing up through the warm blue shells.
Papa Robin sits on the fence, not far away. He doesn't say anything. He just sits. Sometimes he turns his head - left, right, left - watching the yard, the barn, the lane. Keeping watch.
The crickets start. Chirp, chirp, chirp - like a thousand small clocks winding themselves for the night.
The old dog on the porch sighs - a big, round, contented sigh - and puts his head on his paws.
The barn owl, who lives in the hole in the barn's peak, opens one yellow eye. Checks the yard. Closes it. All's well.
Mama Robin shifts her weight. The eggs roll, just a tiny bit, settling deeper into the warmth.
Thump. Thump. Thump. Thump. Four eggs. Four heartbeats. One nest.
The moon comes up over the maple. It comes up slow and round and silver, like a dinner plate someone left in the sky.
The moonlight comes through the leaves and makes dappled patterns on the ground - round, bright spots that move when the wind moves, like they're alive.
Mama Robin's eyes close. Her beak tucks under her wing. But her body stays warm, and her heart keeps counting.
Thump. One. Thump. Two. Thump. Three. Thump. Four.

Someday soon, those four thumps will become four beaks, tapping from the inside. And the shells will crack - tik, tik, tik - and four small mouths will open, and four small voices will say, in their own way: 'I'm here. I'm here. I'm here.'
But not yet. Not tonight.
Tonight, it's just Mama Robin, and the eggs, and the moon, and the counting.
Thump. Thump. Thump. Thump.
Goodnight, maple. Goodnight, moon. Goodnight, four small hearts, beating in the dark.

title: 云的口袋里装着梦（胎教期）
preview: 天上有一朵很软很软的云。它长得像一只懒洋洋的猫，整天在天空里慢慢地飘。云有一个口袋。口袋里装的不是雨，不是雪，是梦...
moral: 有一个梦在等你，从你还没来就开始等了。它空空的，扁扁的，专门留给你。等你来了，你的第一个梦就会装进去——那个梦会是全世界最干净、最温柔的，因为你的心还什么都没碰过。
content: 天上有一朵很软很软的云。
它长得像一只懒洋洋的猫，整天在天空里慢慢地飘。
云有一个口袋。口袋里装的不是雨，不是雪，是梦。
每一朵云都有一个口袋，都装着梦。梦是透明的，软软的，像棉花糖化开以后的样子。
这朵云的口袋里，有一个特别小的梦。别的梦都圆滚滚的，它却扁扁的，像还没有装满。
云问它：「你怎么这么小呀？」
小梦说：「因为我还在等一个人。那个人的梦还没做完，我才能装满。」
「等谁？」
小梦不说话了。它趴在口袋边沿上，往下看。
它看见了一栋小房子。窗户亮着。里面有一位妈妈，拍着圆圆的肚子，嘴里哼着歌。
小梦的眼睛亮了：「就是他。」
「他还没出生呢。」云说。
「我知道。所以我还不能装满。我得等他来了，把他做的梦一点一点装进来。他的第一个梦，一定很小很小，小到只有一粒沙那么大。但那个梦会是最干净的，最软的，因为他的心还什么都没碰过。」
云想了想，说：「那你慢慢等。我飘得慢一点。」
于是云飘啊飘，飘过了山岗，飘过了河流，飘过了一片又一片田野。它飘得特别慢，慢到地上的老鹰都笑话它：「你这是什么云呐，比蜗牛还慢！」
云不理它。云知道，口袋里有一个小梦在等，所以不能颠簸，不能跑太快，不然梦会洒出来的。
每天晚上，云都会飘到那栋小房子的上空，停下来。小梦从口袋边沿往下看，看见妈妈在拍肚子，看见灯灭了，看见月亮升起来了。
有一天，妈妈拍着拍着，肚子动了一下。
小梦激动地抖了抖：「他动了！他是不是在做梦了？」
云笑了：「也许吧。也许他在梦里翻了个身。」
小梦等着。它知道，等那个小宝宝来到这个世界，它的第一个梦就会装进自己的身体里。到那时候，它就不扁了，它就圆了，就饱满了。
而且它知道，那个梦会是全世界最温柔的梦——因为那个梦的主人，还没有见过这个世界的任何一丁点儿不好。
在他看来，一切都是新的，一切都是好的，一切都值得放进梦里。
小梦耐心地等着。云耐心地飘着。月亮耐心地亮着。
它们都在等同一个孩子。

title: The Snuggle Bug Who Couldn't Sleep (Prenatal)
preview: In the crumbly-crumbly corner of the Snuggle-Bug Wood, where the softest of mosses grow soft as they could, there lived a small Snuggle Bug - name of Piddle-dee-Pip - who could NOT get to sleep, not a wink, not a bit!...
moral: Sleep is shy. You can't chase it. But if you hold something soft, and listen to a hum, and stop trying so hard - it'll come. It always comes, when you stop chasing and start being.
content: In the crumbly-crumbly corner of the Snuggle-Bug Wood, where the softest of mosses grow soft as they could, there lived a small Snuggle Bug - name of Piddle-dee-Pip - who could NOT get to sleep, not a wink, not a bit!

'Oh BOTHER and FUSS!' said Piddle-dee-Pip. 'I've wiggled and jiggled and turned and I've flipped! I've counted the stars - I got up to eleven! I've counted the clouds - I ran out at seven! I've tried sleeping on leaves, I've tried sleeping on bark, I've tried sleeping upside down in the dark!'
But nothing worked. Piddle-dee-Pip's eyes were WIDE open. Like two small round windows with nobody home in them.
Along came a friend - a big fuzzy Bear - name of Humphrey-dee-Doo, with fur everywhere, and a smile like a warm honey bun, and a voice like a kettle that's just about done.

'Why, Piddle-dee-Pip! You're still AWAKE?' said Humphrey-dee-Doo, with a worried sort of shake. 'The moon's been up for an HOUR at least! The fireflies have gone to their small firefly feast! The crickets have sung all their cricket-y songs! What's keeping you up when the whole world's gone wrong?'

'I don't KNOW!' said Piddle, and sniffled a bit. 'I'm tired - I'm SO tired - but sleep just won't sit! It flies away! It runs away! It hides behind the tree! I chase it and chase it, but it won't come to me!'

Humphrey-dee-Doo sat down with a THUMP. He folded his big fuzzy arms in a lump. He thought and he thought and he thought some more, and his thinking made the sound of a low gentle snore - which was ironic, but Piddle didn't notice, on account of being too busy being upset.
'I've got it!' said Humphrey, and his eyes went all bright. 'You're chasing sleep, and sleep doesn't like to be chased!'
'It doesn't?' said Piddle.
'No!' said Humphrey. 'Sleep is shy. Sleep comes when you're not looking. Sleep comes when you're so busy NOT-chasing that you forget you were trying!'

'But how do I NOT-chase something I'm trying to chase?' asked Piddle, who was confused, which is a perfectly reasonable way to feel when a bear tells you to stop chasing something you've been chasing all night.
'Easy,' said Humphrey. 'You do something else. Something warm. Something soft. Something that has nothing to do with sleeping.'
'Like what?'
'Like...' Humphrey looked around. He picked up a small handful of moss. He put it in Piddle's hands. 'Feel this.'
Piddle felt it. It was soft. Very, very soft. Like the top of a kitten's head, if the kitten was made of green.
'Now close your eyes,' said Humphrey, 'and just feel the moss. Don't think about sleeping. Don't think about stars. Don't think about counting or clouds or anything. Just... feel.'
Piddle closed his eyes. He felt the moss. It was soft. It was warm. It was there.
Humphrey started to hum. Hmmmm... hmmmm... hmmmm... Not a song. Just a hum. Like a bumblebee that's too tired to buzz.
Piddle felt the moss. He heard the hum. He felt the warm. He felt the close.
And something happened.
Sleep didn't come running. Sleep didn't come flying. Sleep just... settled. Like a leaf on still water. Like snow on a mitten. Like a small warm thing finding a warm soft place and deciding to stay.
Piddle's breathing went slow. Piddle's hands went loose. The moss slipped to the ground - plop - but Piddle didn't notice.
Humphrey smiled. He tucked his big fuzzy arm around Piddle, and he kept humming. Hmmmm... hmmmm... hmmmm...

And the moon, who'd been watching the whole thing from up in the sky, smiled too. Because the moon knows a thing or two about patience. The moon takes all night to cross the sky, and it never hurries, and it always gets there.
'Goodnight, Piddle-dee-Pip,' said Humphrey, very soft.
'Goodnight, Humphrey-dee-Doo,' said the moon, even softer.
And the Snuggle-Bug Wood went quiet - all except the hum.

title: 梦还没来（胎教期）
preview: 后来啊，有一只小猫，叫兜兜。兜兜有一个特别的本事——它能看见梦。人的梦，在人的头顶上飘着，五颜六色的。小孩的梦是粉的，大人的梦是灰的，老人的梦是金的...
moral: 你的第一个梦，正从天上慢慢飘来。它一路收集了风、露水、月光和鸟叫。等你来到这个世界，那个梦就到了——它是全世界最干净、最香的梦，因为它为你攒了一路的温柔。
content: 后来啊，有一只小猫，叫兜兜。兜兜有一个特别的本事——它能看见梦。
人的梦，在人的头顶上飘着，五颜六色的。小孩的梦是粉的，大人的梦是灰的，老人的梦是金的。
可兜兜发现了一件怪事。森林边上的小房子里，那位妈妈肚子里的宝宝——他的头顶上，什么也没有。
兜兜歪着脑袋想了半天。别人的头顶上都有梦，怎么这个宝宝没有呢？
它跑去问猫头鹰爷爷。猫头鹰爷爷整天坐在树洞里，什么都知道。
「猫头鹰爷爷，那个还没出生的小宝宝，头顶上怎么没有梦呢？」
猫头鹰爷爷睁开一只眼睛：「他的梦还没来呢。」
「没来？梦也会迟到？」
「不是迟到。」猫头鹰爷爷慢悠悠地说，「是他的梦还在路上。你看——」
猫头鹰爷爷用翅膀往天上一指。兜兜抬头一看，哎呀！天上有一团特别小特别小的光，正慢慢地、慢慢地往下飘。那团光比萤火虫还小，比蒲公英的绒毛还轻。
「那是他的梦。」猫头鹰爷爷说，「每个宝宝的梦都是从天上来的。梦要飘很久很久，才能飘到宝宝头顶上。」
「为什么这么慢呀？」
「因为梦在路上要收集东西。它要收集一阵风，收集一滴露水，收集一片月光，收集一声鸟叫。收集够了，才能变成一个完整的梦。那个梦才够香，够甜，够软。」
兜兜想帮忙。它跳到屋顶上，对着天上的那团小光喊：「嘿——快点下来！宝宝快出生了！」
小光没理它。它还是慢慢地飘，好像在说：急什么，好东西得慢慢来。
兜兜只好等着。每天晚上，它趴在屋顶上，看着那团小光近了一点点，又近了一点点。
有一天晚上，小光终于飘到了小房子的上空。它在屋顶上停了停，好像在喘口气。
兜兜激动地竖起尾巴：「到了到了！」
小光慢慢地从烟囱里钻进去——兜兜觉得这太冒险了，万一被烟熏黑了怎么办——不过小光没事，它是梦，不怕烟。
小光飘进了卧室，飘到了妈妈的肚子上，然后轻轻一闪，不见了。
兜兜趴在屋顶上，等了一会儿。
然后，它看见了。妈妈的肚子上方，出现了一个很小很小的、粉色的梦。扁扁的，软软的，像一小朵棉花糖。
那是宝宝的第一个梦。
兜兜笑了。猫头鹰爷爷在树洞里也笑了。
你猜宝宝的第一个梦是什么？兜兜看不见梦里的内容，但它看见那个梦的颜色——是全世界最浅最浅的粉，像刚出生的朝霞，像还没被碰过的花瓣。
那颜色，干净得让人心里发软。

title: The Toymaker's Last Song (Prenatal)
preview: There was once a toymaker who lived at the end of a lane that nobody walked down anymore, in a shop that leaned slightly to the left, like a man who'd been standing for a very long time and had gotten tired...
moral: Some songs aren't written yet. They're waiting for the right person to arrive - someone who hasn't been born, maybe, but who's already listening. When you get here, there'll be a song with your name on it. You just have to be ready to hear it.
content: There was once a toymaker who lived at the end of a lane that nobody walked down anymore, in a shop that leaned slightly to the left, like a man who'd been standing for a very long time and had gotten tired.
His name was Mr. Coggle, and he was very old. He'd been making toys for so long that his fingers looked like the wooden dolls he made - knobbly and smooth and worn at the joints.

Mr. Coggle had made every kind of toy you could think of. Clockwork trains. Spinning tops. Jack-in-the-boxes that popped with a satisfying BOING. Dolls with eyes that opened and closed. Tin soldiers that marched. A music box that played a tune so beautiful it made grown men stand still in the street with a faraway look, which was very inconvenient if they happened to be carrying groceries.
But there was one toy Mr. Coggle had never made. He'd been saving the materials for it for forty years.

The materials were: a piece of cedar from his grandmother's hope chest, a brass spring he'd found in a clock when he was nine, a scrap of velvet from his mother's old dress, and a single hair from the head of the woman he'd loved, who had gone away a long, long time ago and taken all the music with her.
'What kind of toy is it?' asked the cat, who was orange and fat and had no business being in the shop, but was there anyway, because cats don't ask permission.
'It's not a toy, exactly,' said Mr. Coggle. He was shaping the cedar with a small knife, very carefully, the way you'd shape something that mattered. 'It's more of a... a song, in a box.'
'A music box?'
'No. A music box plays a song that's already been written. This plays a song that hasn't been written yet. A song for someone who hasn't heard it yet.'
The cat narrowed its eyes. Cats are suspicious of things they don't understand, which is most things.

Mr. Coggle worked all day and all night. He carved the cedar into a small, round box, smooth as an egg. He wound the brass spring inside, but he didn't attach it to any mechanism. He lined the inside with the velvet. And he wove the single hair - which was dark and fine and still smelled faintly of lavender - around the spring, like a thread around a spindle.
When he was done, the box sat on his workbench. It didn't do anything. It didn't play. It didn't open. It just sat there, looking like a small wooden egg, and doing a very good job of it.
'Well?' said the cat. 'Does it work?'
'It's not for me,' said Mr. Coggle. 'It's for someone who hasn't arrived yet.'
'Who?'

'I don't know,' said Mr. Coggle. And the strangest thing was - he smiled when he said it. A real smile, the kind that crinkles the corners of your eyes and makes you look, for a moment, like a young man instead of an old one.
He put the box in the window of his shop. And there it sat.
Weeks passed. Nobody came down the lane. Nobody noticed the box. The cat came and went, catching mice and making disapproving faces at things.

Then one evening, a woman walked down the lane. She was round in the middle, the way women are when they're carrying something precious and heavy and almost-ready. She walked slowly, the way you walk when each step is a negotiation with gravity.
She stopped at the window. She saw the box.
She didn't open the door. She didn't go in. She just stood there, looking at the small wooden egg in the window, and she put her hand on her belly, and she smiled.
And the box - the box that didn't play, that didn't open, that just sat there looking like a small wooden egg - hummed.
Just once. A single note. Low and warm and round, like the first note of a song that's going to be very beautiful when it's finished, but isn't finished yet.
The woman heard it. Or maybe she felt it. Or maybe she just knew, the way you know things that you can't explain and shouldn't try to.
Mr. Coggle, inside the shop, heard it too. He closed his eyes. He was very old, and very tired, and he'd been waiting a very long time.
'There you are,' he said, to nobody, or to everybody, or to the note that was hanging in the air like a held breath. 'I've been waiting for you.'
The note faded. The box went quiet. The woman walked on, slowly, back up the lane, into the evening.

But something had changed. The lane didn't look so forgotten. The shop didn't lean quite so far to the left. And the cat, who was sitting in the window where the box had been, was purring - though there was nobody left to hear it.

Well, that's not quite true. There was somebody. Somebody very small, and very new, and very warm, who hadn't been born yet, but who had just heard the first note of a song that would last their whole life.

title: 啾啾的摇篮曲
preview: 森林里住着一只很小很小的小鸟，她的名字叫啾啾。啾啾的个子只有一颗橡果那么大，羽毛是浅浅的鹅黄色，像一朵会飞的小迎春花...
moral: 世界上最温柔的声音，不是最响亮的那一个，而是用心收集、轻轻送出的那一个。你来到这个世界之前，风在等你，水在等你，树叶在等你——它们把最好听的声音攒在一起，编成了一首只属于你的歌。愿你在这首歌里安心入睡，也愿你长大以后，把这份温柔继续唱给身边的人听。
content: 森林里住着一只很小很小的小鸟，她的名字叫啾啾。啾啾的个子只有一颗橡果那么大，羽毛是浅浅的鹅黄色，像一朵会飞的小迎春花。
啾啾有一副好嗓子，森林里的小动物都爱听她唱歌。可啾啾心里一直藏着一个愿望——她想学一首全世界最软、最轻、最温柔的摇篮曲。
大家问她：「你又不是妈妈，为什么要学摇篮曲呢？」啾啾歪着小脑袋，认真地回答：「因为在森林边上的那栋小房子里，有一位妈妈的肚子里，正住着一个还没有出生的小宝宝。我想等他来到这个世界的那一天，送他一首歌。」
啾啾拍拍翅膀，决定出发去寻找最温柔的声音。
她先飞到了山间的小溪旁。小溪从高高的石头上跌下来，溅起一串串水花，「哗啦啦，哗啦啦」地唱着歌。啾啾站在溪边的鹅卵石上，认真地听了好久好久。
「小溪姐姐，你的声音真好听，可不可以借给我一点点？」啾啾问。
小溪笑了起来，水面上泛起一圈一圈的酒窝：「我的声音太活泼啦，小宝宝听了会想蹦蹦跳跳的。不过，你可以把我最安静的那一段带走——就是月亮升起来的时候，我流过水草，『沙沙沙』的那一小段。那是我一天里最轻的声音。」
啾啾高兴地把「沙沙沙」收进了心里。她的胸口暖暖的，像装了一小团柔软的水草。
接着，她飞到了一棵很高很高的老槐树上。老槐树的叶子又多又密，风一吹，就发出「簌簌簌」的声音，像老爷爷在翻一本很旧很旧的书。
「槐树爷爷，您的声音好沉稳，好安心。可不可以借给我一点点？」
老槐树慢悠悠地抖了抖树枝，落下几片叶子，像是在点头：「我的声音太沉啦，小宝宝听了会觉得像在坐船。不过，你可以把我傍晚的那一段带走——就是晚风刚刚起来的时候，我的叶子互相说悄悄话，『窸窸窣窣』的那一小段。那是我一天里最温柔的声音。」
啾啾把「窸窸窣窣」也收进了心里。现在她的胸口装了两样东西，一小团水草的声音，和一小把叶子说悄悄话的声音。
最后，她飞到了一片芦苇荡。月光洒在芦苇上，每一根芦苇都亮亮的，像一根银色的琴弦。微风吹过，芦苇们轻轻摇晃，发出「嘘——嘘——」的声音，又轻又长，像是有人在很远很远的地方，吹着一支看不到的竹笛。
啾啾什么也没说，只是安安静静地站在芦苇尖上，闭上眼睛，让那个「嘘——嘘——」的声音，像一条银色的丝线一样，慢慢地绕进了她的心里。
现在，啾啾的心里装了三样东西——小溪的「沙沙沙」，老槐树的「窸窸窣窣」，还有芦苇荡的「嘘——嘘——」。它们混在一起，像一条软软的、暖暖的小毯子，在啾啾的心里轻轻地翻着、卷着。
啾啾试着唱了唱。啊呀，不对。她唱出来的声音太响了，像是在开一场森林音乐会。小宝宝需要的不是音乐会，小宝宝需要的是——一个轻轻的、暖暖的、像被抱在怀里一样的声音。
啾啾有点沮丧。她低着头，飞回了森林边上那栋小房子旁边的老榆树上。月亮已经升得老高老高了，小房子的窗户里，透出昏黄的灯光。
啾啾看见，那位妈妈正坐在摇椅上，一只手轻轻地、慢慢地拍着圆圆的肚子，另一只手翻着一本图画书。她的嘴唇在轻轻地动，好像在给肚子里的小宝宝念一个故事。
啾啾忽然明白了。她明白了为什么小溪说「把最安静的那一段带走」，为什么老槐树说「把傍晚说悄悄话的那一段带走」——因为最温柔的摇篮曲，不是一首很厉害的歌，而是一个人在你身边，轻轻地、慢慢地、不慌不忙地陪着你。
就像妈妈拍肚子的节奏。就像心跳的节奏。
啾啾深吸了一口气，把心里的三样声音揉在一起，揉成了一缕比月光还细的声音。然后，她张开小嘴巴，轻轻地、轻轻地唱了起来——
「沙沙沙」，像水流过水草。「窸窸窣窣」，像叶子说悄悄话。「嘘——嘘——」，像芦苇在月光里摇晃。
这首歌没有词，只有声音。可这些声音拼在一起，刚好是一颗心脏跳动的节奏——「咚，咚，咚，咚」——不快不慢，不轻不重，像一只温柔的手掌，一下一下地，拍着一个小小的、暖暖的后背。
妈妈好像听见了。她抬起头，朝窗外望了望，看见了老榆树枝头那只鹅黄色的小小鸟。她笑了，把窗户推开了一点点缝。
啾啾的歌声就顺着那条缝，像一缕月光一样，轻轻地溜了进去。它绕过窗帘，绕过床头的小台灯，最后落在了妈妈圆圆的肚子上——轻轻地，像一片羽毛。
肚子里的小宝宝动了动。不是那种大大的踢腿，而是一种很轻很轻的、像翻了个身的动。就好像他在妈妈的肚子里，听见了这首歌，然后安心地换了一个更舒服的姿势。
妈妈低下头，摸了摸肚子，眼睛弯弯的，轻声说：「宝宝，你听见了吗？有只小鸟在给你唱摇篮曲呢。她一定飞了好远好远的路，才找到这么温柔的声音。」
啾啾在树枝上听见了这句话，整只鸟都暖烘烘的。她忽然觉得，自己飞过的每一段路，听过的每一种声音，都是为了这一刻——为了把全世界的温柔，编成一首歌，送给一个还没出生的小宝宝。
从那以后，每天晚上，月亮升起来的时候，啾啾都会飞到老榆树上，把那首没有词的摇篮曲，轻轻地唱给小房子听。妈妈会打开窗户，让歌声飘进来，飘到她的肚子上，飘到小宝宝的耳朵里。
小宝宝在歌声里一天一天地长大。他学会了在妈妈肚子里翻跟头，学会了打哈欠，还学会了——在啾啾唱歌的时候，安安静静地、一动不动地，好像在认真地听。
后来有一天，小宝宝出生了。那是个胖乎乎的小家伙，哭声特别响亮。可当护士把他抱到妈妈怀里的时候，他还在哭。
妈妈轻轻地拍着他的后背，可他还在哭。窗外的啾啾急了，她飞到窗台上，用最轻最轻的声音，唱起了那首没有词的摇篮曲——「沙沙沙，窸窸窣窣，嘘——嘘——」
奇迹发生了。小家伙的哭声一点一点地小了下去。他的小拳头松开了，他的小脚丫不蹬了，他的眼睛慢慢地、慢慢地闭上了。他在妈妈怀里，安安静静地睡着了，嘴角还挂着一个很小很小的、像是微笑的弧度。
妈妈抬起头，看见窗台上那只鹅黄色的小鸟，眼眶一下子就红了。她用口型轻轻地说了一句：「谢谢你。」
啾啾歪了歪小脑袋，拍拍翅膀，飞回了森林里。月光洒在她鹅黄色的羽毛上，把她变成了一只会飞的小灯笼。
她想，原来最温柔的摇篮曲，是走遍全世界，把最好的声音收集起来，再轻轻地、轻轻地，放在一个新生命的耳边。
她想，原来每一个来到这个世界的小宝宝，都值得一首专门为他而唱的歌。
而她，一只只有橡果那么大的小鸟，却把整个世界的温柔，都唱进了一首歌里。

title: The Creek That Sang Itself to Sleep (Prenatal)
preview: Down in the hollow where the ferns grow tall, where the stones are all mossy and the water's so small - there runs a creek that goes tinkle-tink-tink, and it runs all day long, and it runs all night, I think...
moral: The world is full of songs that go on without stopping - the creek, the wind, the cricket, the frog. They don't stop for night. They just get softer. And if you listen - really listen - you'll hear them singing you to sleep. They've been singing all along.
content: Down in the hollow where the ferns grow tall, where the stones are all mossy and the water's so small - there runs a creek that goes tinkle-tink-tink, and it runs all day long, and it runs all night, I think.

The creek goes tinkle-tink-tink over the stones. It goes shhhh-shhhh-shhh where the water hits the mud. It goes gurgle-gurgle-gurgle where it passes under the old log bridge, and it goes plip-plop-plip where it drips off the last rock at the end, into the deep pool where the big fish live (well, big for a creek - about the size of your hand).

The creek has a voice. Not a loud voice. Not a show-offy voice. A working voice - the kind of voice that's always there, like the hum of a fridge, like the tick of a clock, like the breathing of someone sleeping next to you.

When the sun goes down behind the ridge, the creek keeps going. Tinkle-tink-tink. It doesn't stop for night. It doesn't know what night is. It just knows: keep going, keep singing, keep moving over the stones.
The fireflies come out. Blink, blink, blink. They land on the ferns by the creek. The ferns don't mind. The creek doesn't mind. Everything by the creek is the not-minding kind.

A raccoon comes down to the water. Dip-dip-dip go his little hands. He's looking for crawfish. He doesn't find any. He doesn't mind. He washes his hands anyway - raccoons are like that, they'll wash their hands whether there's anything to wash them for or not.

The moon comes up. Big and round and slow, like a wheel of cheese rolling across the sky. The moonlight lands on the creek, and the creek turns silver, and the tinkle-tink-tink gets a little bit softer, like even the water wants to be gentle.
The crickets start. Chirp-chirp-chirp. The creek doesn't mind. It adds them to its song. Tinkle-tink-tink-chirp. Shhhh-shhhh-chirp. Gurgle-gurgle-chirp.
The bullfrog says: rummm... rummm... rummm... The creek doesn't mind. It adds that too. Tinkle-tink-rummm. Shhhh-shhh-rummm.

And slowly, slowly, slowly, the creek's song gets softer. And slower. And softer and slower. Until it's not really a song anymore - it's more like a breathing. In and out. Tinkle... shhhh... tinkle... shhhh...
The raccoon falls asleep in the ferns, with his wet little paws tucked under his chin.
The fireflies blink slower and slower and slower, until they're just tiny dots of light that might be stars, or might be reflections, or might be nothing at all.
The creek keeps going. But now it's going slow. Very slow. Like it's walking on tiptoe. Like it's trying not to wake anyone up.
Tinkle... tink... tink...
Shhhh... shhh... shhh...
The moon watches over the hollow. The ferns bend low. The creek breathes in, and breathes out, and breathes in, and breathes out.

And somewhere, not far from the creek, in a house with a warm yellow window, a mother is humming. And the creek hears the humming, and adds it to its song. And the mother hears the creek, and adds it to her hum.
And two songs become one song. And the one song becomes sleep.

title: 露珠邮递员（胎教期）
preview: 天还没亮透的时候，竹林里每一片叶子上都住着一个小小的露珠邮递员。他们背着亮晶晶的小包裹，排成细细的队伍，沿着叶脉往下滑。
moral: 世界上最美的等待，就是知道有人正穿过晨雾、越过山岗，只为把温柔送到你身边。
content: 天还没亮透的时候，竹林里每一片叶子上都住着一个小小的露珠邮递员。他们背着亮晶晶的小包裹，排成细细的队伍，沿着叶脉往下滑——吧嗒，吧嗒，吧嗒——像一串没有声音的铃铛。
最小的那个露珠邮递员叫小晶晶。她是昨晚的月色凝成的，圆溜溜的，透明的，风一吹就轻轻晃一晃，像一颗会呼吸的珍珠。今天轮到小晶晶送信——一封从山那边寄来的信，信封上画了一朵云，云里面写着："收信人——住在竹林东边第一个鸟窝下方第三片草叶上的妈妈。"
小晶晶深深吸了一口气——她吸的是晨雾的味道，凉凉的、甜甜的，还有一点点竹叶的清香。"走啦！"她对自己说，然后沿着叶脉往下滑——咕噜咕噜，咕噜咕噜——像坐滑梯一样，一直滑到叶尖尖上。
叶尖尖下面是一片苔藓，软软的、绿绿的，像一块绿色的小地毯。小晶晶跳了下去——啪——在苔藓上弹了弹，没有碎，稳稳地站住了。她开心地晃了晃身体，亮晶晶的水光在苔藓上一闪一闪的。
接下来要爬过一块大石头。石头上有细细的纹路，像老爷爷额头上的皱纹。小晶晶一步一步，小心地绕过那些纹路。有一道纹路里住着三只蚂蚁，它们正在做早操——"一二三四，二二三四"——看见小晶晶，都停了下来。"你背着的是什么呀？"最小的那只蚂蚁问。小晶晶挺了挺圆鼓鼓的身子，说："是一封很重要的信，要送给草叶上的妈妈。"三只蚂蚁齐声说："那你快去吧，我们帮你把前面的路扫干净。"
蚂蚁们用触角把小路上的尘土扫开，小晶晶顺利地走了过去。"谢谢你们！"她回头喊了一声，亮晶晶的身体在阳光里闪着七彩的光。
然后是穿过一片枯叶。枯叶是去年秋天落下来的，已经变成了褐色，上面有虫虫咬出的小洞洞。小晶晶从一个小洞里钻过去——啵——身体被洞口挤成了椭圆形，过了洞口又弹回圆圆的形状，好玩极了。枯叶下面藏着一只小蜗牛，正在慢悠悠地吃早餐。"嗨，小露珠，你这么急去哪儿呀？"蜗牛慢吞吞地问，一个字还没说完，小晶晶已经从另一个洞洞里钻出去了。
终于到了一片矮矮的草丛。小晶晶数着："第一片草叶，第二片草叶，第三片草叶——就是这里！"第三片草叶的根部长着一朵小小的野菊花，菊花的旁边，一位妈妈正静静地坐着。她不是人类的妈妈，是一只纺织娘。纺织娘妈妈的怀里抱着六颗淡绿色的小小的卵，她用薄薄的翅膀轻轻地盖着它们，嘴里哼着温柔的曲子："睡吧，睡吧，我的小宝贝，风在林子外面等着呢，等你们醒来，它就带你们去看世界……"
小晶晶屏住呼吸——她怕自己"啵"的一声破了——慢慢地、慢慢地靠近。她走到纺织娘妈妈的脚边，把背上的小包裹递了过去。小包裹在空气中自己展开了——原来里面装着的不是信纸，而是一小段歌声。那歌声从山那边飘过来的，是一个爸爸的声音，他唱着和纺织娘妈妈一模一样的曲子："睡吧，睡吧，我的小宝贝，我在山这边等着呢……"
纺织娘妈妈听着听着，眼睛湿润了。她低下头，看见脚边小小的露珠邮递员，小晶晶已经快要被太阳晒得透明了，却还努力地举着那封歌声信。"谢谢你，小晶晶。"纺织娘妈妈说，然后把那首歌又唱了一遍，唱给怀里的六颗小卵听，也唱给已经快要蒸发了的小晶晶听。
小晶晶听着听着，觉得自己变轻了、变淡了，慢慢升了起来，升到草叶上空，升到竹林的顶上，变成了一缕看不见的水汽。但她很开心——因为她知道，那封信已经送到了。那位妈妈和那六颗还没出生的小宝宝，都听到了从山那边飘来的歌。
第二天的清晨，竹林里又结出了新的露珠。其中有一颗圆圆的小露珠，在叶尖上醒来的时候，发现自己背上已经有一个亮晶晶的小包裹在等她了。下一个邮递员继续出发。吧嗒，吧嗒，吧嗒——穿过晨雾，越过山岗，把温柔送到每一个等待的角落。

title: The Little Brook That Learned to Wait (Prenatal)
preview: Way up in the rolling hills, where the morning mist curled like sleepy cats around the oak trees, there lived a tiny brook. She was so small that a squirrel could hop across her in one leap.
moral: Some things take time to arrive, and the waiting itself is part of the gift. A gentle heart that learns to wait learns to love.
content: Way up in the rolling hills, where the morning mist curled like sleepy cats around the oak trees, there lived a tiny brook. She was so small that a squirrel could hop across her in one leap, and her water ran so softly that you had to bend down very close to hear her sing: trickle-trickle, hush-hush, trickle-trickle, hush-hush.

The little brook had a job. Every morning, she carried messages from the top of the hill down to the valley below. A fallen petal from the wild rose bushes — that was a hello from the hilltop. A tiny pebble, smoothed round by the water — that was a story from somewhere upstream. The brook carried them all, trickle-trickle, hush-hush, never rushing, never stopping.

One misty morning, the oldest oak tree on the hill leaned down — creak, creak, creak — and whispered to the brook. 'Little one,' said the oak, his voice like wind through old branches, 'there is something special coming to the valley. Something small. Something new. Something that has never been here before. Could you wait for it?'
The little brook had never been asked to wait before. She was always moving, always flowing, always going somewhere. 'Wait?' she bubbled. 'How do you wait when you are made of running water?'

The old oak smiled — his bark crinkled like a thousand tiny smiles all at once. 'You wait by being gentle,' he said. 'You wait by singing softly. You wait by noticing every little thing along the way.'

So the little brook tried. She slowed her water to the gentlest trickle — barely a whisper, just enough to keep moving. She sang her quietest song: trickle... trickle... hush... hush... And she began to notice things she had never noticed before.

She noticed that the moss on her stones had tiny silver tips that caught the morning light. She noticed that a water beetle had built a nest under her bank — a little dome of mud and bubbles, with tiny beetle eggs inside, each one smaller than a pinhead. She noticed that when the sun hit her water at just the right angle, she made rainbows — not big shouting rainbows, but tiny quiet ones, no bigger than a baby's fingernail, that danced on the pebbles.

Day after day, the brook waited. Trickle-trickle, hush-hush. The wild roses bloomed and dropped their petals. The water beetle's eggs hatched into tiny swimming specks. The oak tree's leaves turned from spring-green to deep summer-green. And still the brook waited. She did not know what she was waiting for, exactly. But she trusted the old oak, and she trusted the waiting itself.

Then one evening, when the sky was the color of a ripening blueberry and the first star was just blinking awake, something changed. The air grew soft — softer than it had ever been. The wind stopped and held its breath. Even the crickets paused their night song for one long, hushed moment.

And then the brook heard it. A tiny sound. Not from the water, not from the wind, not from any creature in the valley. It came from a little house at the edge of the meadow. A sound so small that only someone who had been waiting — really waiting — could hear it.
Waaaaaaah. Waaaaaaah. A baby's first cry.

The little brook trembled with joy. Her water sparkled brighter than it had ever sparkled before. She wanted to rush down and see — but she remembered: be gentle. So she flowed, slow and soft, down the last stretch of hill, carrying a wild rose petal and a smooth round pebble as her welcome gifts. Trickle-trickle, hush-hush, welcome-to-the-world, welcome-to-the-world.

The old oak watched from the hilltop, his branches swaying in a breeze that felt like a blessing. 'You see,' he whispered to the night, 'the brook learned what the river never could. Some things are worth slowing down for.'

And every night after that, the little brook sang her quietest lullaby — trickle-trickle, hush-hush — flowing past the little house at the edge of the meadow, carrying her song to the baby who was learning to sleep under the stars. Trickle-trickle, hush-hush. Sleep, little one, sleep.

title: 月亮爷爷巡夜（胎教期）
preview: 孩子们，你们知道吗？每天晚上，等你们都睡下了，月亮爷爷就要出来巡夜啦。他提着一盏银灯笼，慢悠悠地走过山岗，走过小河，走过你家的窗台。
moral: 每一份安宁都不是凭空而来的。月亮爷爷的巡夜告诉我们：世界上总有人在你看不到的地方，悄悄地守护着你。就像妈妈怀着你的时候，她的心跳、她的呼吸、她轻声哼的歌，都是为你巡夜的银灯笼。你不必害怕黑暗，因为爱，一直在你身边走着。
content: 孩子们，你们知道吗？每天晚上，等你们都睡下了，月亮爷爷就要出来巡夜啦。他提着一盏银灯笼，慢悠悠地走过山岗，走过小河，走过你家的窗台。他的脚步很轻很轻，轻得连风都听不见。
月亮爷爷先走到山坡上。小草们正歪着脑袋打瞌睡呢，有的还嘟嘟囔囔地说梦话。月亮爷爷把灯笼往低处放了放，银色的光像水一样淌下来，淌过每一片叶子。小草们觉得暖融融的，翻了个身，睡得更香了。
咕咚——咕咚——山脚下的小溪还在流。月亮爷爷蹲下来，对着小溪说：'小溪呀小溪，天黑了，你也该歇歇了。'小溪说：'月亮爷爷，我停不下来呀，我得给下游的小鱼送水去。'月亮爷爷笑了笑，从灯笼里拨出一点光，撒在小溪水面上。溪水一下子亮闪闪的，像铺了一条银被子。小溪流着流着，声音越来越小，越来越小，最后变成细细的、柔柔的'沙沙沙'，像在唱催眠曲。
月亮爷爷又走到老槐树跟前。老槐树已经一百多岁了，胡子（就是那些气根）拖得老长老长。知了在树上睡得正沉，偶尔'吱——'叫半声，又没音了。月亮爷爷轻轻拍了拍老槐树的树干：'老伙计，夜深了。'老槐树的叶子沙沙响了几下，像在说：'嗯，知道了。'然后整棵树安安静静的，一动也不动。
走着走着，月亮爷爷来到一扇窗前。窗里头，有一位妈妈正侧着身子睡，手轻轻搭在肚子上。肚子里有个小宝宝，还没出生呢。月亮爷爷把灯笼贴近窗户，银光透过玻璃，柔柔地洒在妈妈的肚子上。
小宝宝在里头动了动。他感觉到了——那光暖暖的，像妈妈的手掌，像爸爸的声音，像外面的风和溪水混在一起的味道。小宝宝不知道那是什么，但他觉得安全，觉得踏实，又安静地蜷起来。
月亮爷爷站在窗外，看了好一会儿。他没说话，只是把灯笼举得更高一些，让光更均匀地铺满整间屋子。然后他踮起脚，悄悄地走了。
吧嗒，吧嗒。这是月亮爷爷的脚步声吗？不是的，孩子们。月亮爷爷走路是没有声音的。那是什么？那是远处的小青蛙，在池塘边数星星呢——一颗、两颗、三颗……数着数着，自己也打了个哈欠，扑通一声跳进水里，睡了。
月亮爷爷走啊走，走过田野，走过竹林，走过每一户亮着灯的和灭了灯的人家。走到天边的时候，他回头望了一眼——整个世界都安安静静的。小草睡了，小溪睡了，知了睡了，老槐树睡了，妈妈睡了，宝宝也睡了。
月亮爷爷笑了笑，把灯笼别在腰间，自己也坐到云朵上，打了个哈欠。'嗯，今晚的夜，巡完了。'
孩子们，下次你睡不着的时候，就想想月亮爷爷。他提着银灯笼，正从你的窗前经过呢。他不会吵你，只是悄悄地看你一眼，把一点银光留在你的枕头边。然后你就会觉得——嗯，暖暖的，软软的，可以睡了。

title: The Robin Who Counted Stars (Prenatal)
preview: In the old maple tree by the stone wall, Mrs. Robin had a nest. It was a fine nest, round and soft, made of dried grass and mud and the softest bits of moss she could find.
moral: Even before we arrive, we are already loved. Mrs. Robin counting the stars for her unhatched chicks reminds us that the world prepares a place for us before we even know it exists. Every lullaby sung to an unborn child, every gentle word whispered in the dark, is like a star being counted - a small light saved up, waiting to welcome us home.
content: In the old maple tree by the stone wall, Mrs. Robin had a nest. It was a fine nest, round and soft, made of dried grass and mud and the softest bits of moss she could find. She had worked on it for three whole days, flying back and forth, back and forth, until her wings ached and her beak was tired.

Now the nest was ready, and in it lay three small eggs, blue as the evening sky. Mrs. Robin sat on them carefully, tucking her warm feathers around them like a blanket. She could feel them beneath her - smooth and cool and full of promise.

Kuplink. Kuplank. Kuplunk. That was the sound of a berry dropping into a tin pail somewhere down the hill. Mrs. Robin cocked her head. That would be old Mr. McCracken, picking blueberries in the twilight, the way he did every summer evening. She had watched him from this very tree last summer, when she was just a fledgling herself.
The sun went down behind the ridge, and the sky turned from gold to rose to deep, deep blue. One by one, the stars came out - first one, then three, then seven, then too many to count.
But Mrs. Robin tried anyway.

'One,' she said softly, looking at the brightest one. 'Two.' She found another, just above the steeple of the white church. 'Three.' There was one peeking through the branches of the pine tree. 'Four, five, six...' She counted slowly, in a whisper, the way you count sheep when you cannot sleep.
Her eggs did not move. They did not cheep or wiggle. But Mrs. Robin counted the stars for them anyway, the way a mother hums a lullaby to a child who has not yet learned to listen.

Down below, the creek murmured its nighttime song - shush, shush, shush - like a brook clearing its throat before bedtime. A bullfrog in the mill pond said 'br-r-rump' once, then thought better of it and closed his mouth. The fireflies came out, drifting among the cattails like tiny lanterns, like the stars had come down to visit the ground.

Mrs. Robin counted the fireflies too. 'Seven, eight, nine...' But they kept moving, and she lost track. She ruffled her feathers in a small huff. 'Well,' she said to her eggs, 'I suppose stars are easier. They stay where you put them.'

A breeze came up from the south, warm and smelling of hay and clover. It rustled through the maple leaves above her head - shhh, shhh, shhh - as if the tree itself were saying 'hush.' Mrs. Robin settled deeper into her nest. The eggs were warm. The night was kind. The stars were out.

She counted three more stars - 'ten, eleven, twelve' - and then her eyes grew heavy. The numbers started to blur together. Twelve became twenty. Twenty became a hundred. A hundred became just... light. Soft, silver light, falling through the leaves like rain.
'Thirteen,' she murmured, her beak barely moving. 'Four... teen...'
And then Mrs. Robin was asleep, and the stars kept watch for her.

In the morning, the sun would come up and dry the dew on the grass, and Mr. McCracken would come out with his pail, kuplink, kuplank, kuplunk, and the world would be busy and bright again. But for now, in the old maple tree by the stone wall, three small blue eggs waited in their warm nest, and their mother counted stars for them in her dreams.
And the stars, patient and old, did not mind being counted. They had been waiting a very long time to be noticed by someone small and new. They could wait a little longer.

title: 月光小船（胎教期）
preview: 在银河的最深处，那里没有白天，只有温柔的夜晚。银河的水面上，漂着一艘小小的船——月光小船。
moral: 等待不是空白的时间，而是爱在静静生长。月光小船收集的每一句悄悄话，都是妈妈种下的一颗种子。宝宝虽然还看不见这个世界，但世界已经把所有的温柔都准备好了——在月光里，在风里，在每一个宁静的夜晚里。
content: 在银河的最深处，那里没有白天，只有温柔的夜晚。银河的水面像一匹无边无际的深蓝色绸缎，上面缀满了碎钻石一样的星星。水面上，漂着一艘小小的船。
这艘船小到什么程度呢？小到一片月光刚好铺满它的船底，小到一只萤火虫落在船头，整艘船就会轻轻往下沉一沉。它叫「月光小船」，是用月亮最温柔的那一束光编织而成的。船身泛着淡淡的银白色，像妈妈手指尖的温度，软软的、暖暖的。
每天晚上，当人间的灯火一盏一盏熄灭，月光小船就从银河的尽头出发了。撑船的是个白胡子老爷爷，他的胡须长极了，垂到水面上，被星光染成了淡银色。他不是别人，正是月亮爷爷——白天他在天上睡觉，晚上他就变成了月光小船的老船夫。
月亮爷爷撑着船，从银河的东边划到西边。他不捕鱼，不捞虾，他有一个世界上最温柔的工作——收集悄悄话。
什么是悄悄话呢？就是每一位妈妈在夜里对肚子里宝宝说的话。有的妈妈说：'宝宝，妈妈今天吃了你最爱吃的草莓。'有的妈妈说：'宝宝，爸爸今天给你买了一件小衣裳，上面绣着一只小兔子。'有的妈妈什么也不说，只是把手轻轻放在肚子上，一下一下地抚摸——那也是悄悄话，只是不用嘴巴说，用心说。
这些悄悄话啊，像蒲公英的种子一样，乘着晚风轻轻地飘起来，飘过屋顶，飘过树梢，飘到银河里，变成一粒一粒小小的光点。月亮爷爷就用月光小船的船头轻轻地接住它们——叮，叮，叮——每接住一颗，船底就会闪一下温柔的亮光。
在这些悄悄话里，有一颗特别特别亮的。它是从一座开满栀子花的小院子里飘来的。那里的窗户半开着，白色的纱帘被风吹得一鼓一鼓，像一个在呼吸的梦。窗户后面，住着一位妈妈和一个小宝宝——正在妈妈肚子里慢慢长大的你。
妈妈的悄悄话是这样飘来的：她坐在窗前，手里拿着一个小小的针线篮，里面有一块柔软的棉布，上面绣了一半的小星星。她的手指很慢很慢地缝着，心里想的是：等宝宝来了，就用这块布做一个小枕头，让宝宝天天枕着星星睡觉。
她没有说出声，但她的心在说话。那声音比风吹过风铃还轻，比露珠从草尖滑落还安静——咕噜噜，咕噜噜。月亮爷爷却听到了，他把船靠过去，用胡须尖儿轻轻一碰，那颗悄悄话就落进了船舱里。
月亮爷爷把悄悄话装进一只小小的贝壳里。这只贝壳是他在银河底找到的，通体半透明，里面仿佛有一层薄薄的珍珠粉。他把贝壳合上，放在月光小船最安全的那只小篮子里。篮子里已经有好几十只这样的贝壳了，每一只里都装着一句妈妈的悄悄话。
啵——啵——啵——那些贝壳轻轻碰撞着，发出珍珠滚动般的声音。它们都在等同一件事：等宝宝出生的那一天。
那一天到来的时候，月光小船会从银河一路漂到人间。月亮爷爷会打开每一只贝壳，所有妈妈的悄悄话会像萤火虫一样飞出来，绕着宝宝的摇篮轻轻地飞，飞成一条闪光的河。那时候，宝宝虽然还不能听懂话，但会闻到妈妈的爱，闻到栀子花的香，闻到银河里星星的味道——那味道啊，像甜甜的米糊，又像凉凉的夜风。
而那只从栀子花小院飘来的贝壳，打开后会变成一个最甜的梦。梦里有一个妈妈，坐在窗前，正在绣一颗小星星。她的手指很慢，但每一针都准准的，因为每一针都是爱。
等待的日子一天天过去。有时候月亮爷爷也会把船停在一片云的后面，静静地看一看那座小院子。栀子花谢了又开，开了又谢，妈妈的肚子一天比一天圆，像一个小小的地球仪，里面装着一个小小的宇宙。
月亮爷爷看着看着，胡须会笑得翘起来。他活了很久很久，见过成千上万个宝宝来到这个世界。但他从来没有看腻。因为每一个宝宝，都是这世界上独一无二的一颗小星星。每一句悄悄话，都是这银河里唯一的一道光。
今晚，月光小船又出发了。月亮爷爷撑着船，桨在水面上划出银色的涟漪——哗啦，哗啦——像时间轻柔的脚步。他要去接新的悄悄话了。也许，你的妈妈的悄悄话正在路上呢。
闭上眼睛吧，小宝贝。在你的小宇宙里翻个身，打个小小的哈欠。月光小船正从你的窗外经过——不，它不会吵你，它只是路过，把你的名字记在老船夫的那本星星册子里。等你来的那一天，月亮爷爷会第一个告诉你：'嘿，小家伙，银河的船票已经给你准备好啦。'

title: The Little Whispering Stream (Prenatal)
preview: Deep in the quiet meadow, where the grass grows tall and the clover nods in the breeze, there ran a little stream. It was not a big stream. It was not a loud stream.
moral: Some of the sweetest songs are the ones we cannot hear yet. The stream did not know who it was singing to, but it sang anyway - the way a mother hums to a baby months before that baby can hear. Love does not wait for an answer. It begins long before the hello.
content: Deep in the quiet meadow, where the grass grows tall and the clover nods in the breeze, there ran a little stream. It was not a big stream. It was not a loud stream. It was the kind of stream a rabbit could hop across in one jump - boing! - and a fawn could wade through without the water reaching its knees.

Every evening, just as the sun dipped behind the ridge and the sky turned the color of peach fuzz, the little stream began to whisper. Shush-shush. Trickle-trickle. Plip-plop-plip. It was a song that had no words, but somehow it said everything.

The stream had been singing this song for as long as anyone could remember. It sang to the cattails that grew along its banks - swish, swish - and they swayed in time. It sang to the dragonflies with their wings like spun glass - skitter-skatter - and they danced above the water. It sang to the fat old bullfrog who lived under the mossy log - croak-croak, ribbit-ribbit - and he blinked his golden eyes and listened.
But the stream had a secret. There was someone it wanted very much to sing to. Someone who was not a cattail, or a dragonfly, or even a bullfrog.

This someone lived in a little white house on the hill, just above the meadow. The house had a red door and a porch swing that creaked in the wind - eee-ahh, eee-ahh. And inside the house lived a mama and... someone very small.

The stream had heard about this someone from the wind. The wind was a great traveler - it went everywhere! It had pushed through the lace curtain of the nursery window and had seen the little crib, the soft blankets, the mobile of wooden stars that turned and turned in the afternoon light. And the wind had felt something else: a warmth so gentle, so patient, that it could only mean one thing. Someone was on their way.
'I must sing to them,' said the little stream. 'I must sing the softest song I know.'
But the stream was down in the meadow, and the house was up on the hill. How could a little stream make its voice travel all that way?
The stream thought and thought. Trickle-trickle. Think-think. And then it had an idea.
'Wind!' called the stream. 'Oh, Wind! Would you carry my song up the hill?'
The wind rustled through the tall grass - whoosh, whoosh - and said, 'Of course, little stream. I carry all sorts of things. Pollen and seeds and the smell of rain. A song is no trouble at all.'

So that evening, when the peach-colored sky began to deepen, the stream sang its very best song. Shush-shush, trickle-trickle, plip-plop-plip. It sang about how the moon reflects on still water, a silver coin that cannot be spent. It sang about how the first crocus pushes through the snow in March - brave little purple thing! It sang about the way a mama deer nudges her spotted fawn to stand up for the very first time.
The wind caught every note and carried it up the hill - whish, whish, whish. Past the cattails. Past the dragonflies. Past the fat old bullfrog who croaked a blessing as the song went by.

The wind slipped through the crack under the red door and spiraled up the stairs. It found the nursery with the lace curtain and the wooden-star mobile. And there, in the quiet room where a mama sat knitting something small and soft, it let the stream's song fall like a gentle rain.
Plip-plop. Shush-shush. Trickle-trickle.
The mama paused her knitting. She tilted her head. 'Do you hear that?' she whispered. But no one answered - at least, not with words.

But the someone very small, the someone growing in the warm dark, felt the song. Not with ears - it was too soon for ears. But with something older, something deeper. The rhythm of the water. The rise and fall of the melody. It was like being rocked, gently, gently, the way the stream rocks a fallen leaf down its course.

Night after night, the stream sent its song up the hill. And night after night, the someone very small grew a little bigger, a little stronger, a little more ready to meet the world. And all the while, the song was there - a thread of silver sound, tying the meadow to the nursery, the stream to the crib, the waiting world to the one who was coming.

Kuplink, kuplank, kuplunk. That was the sound of evening settling over the meadow. The stream's song grew softer, softer, until it was barely a whisper. The bullfrog closed his eyes. The dragonflies folded their wings. The wind, tired from its work, curled up in the pine trees and went to sleep.

And the someone on the hill, who was not quite ready to arrive, drifted into a dream. In the dream, there was water. Warm water. And the gentlest voice saying: shush-shush. Trickle-trickle. Wait for me. I will be here when you come.

The stream keeps singing still, every evening, waiting for the day when the red door will open and someone new will be carried down to the meadow to dip tiny toes in the cool, clear water. On that day, the song will change - it will be louder, happier, full of splashes and giggles. But for now, the little stream whispers. And that is enough.

title: 给风系个铃铛（胎教期）
preview: 傍晚的时候，妈妈坐在窗前，手里拿着一只小小的铃铛。铃铛是铜色的，只有一颗樱桃那么大，系着一根淡粉色的丝带。
moral: 世界不会等小宝贝出生才开始爱他。风在跑，铃在响，麦浪在沙沙，青蛙在唱歌——一切温柔的声音，都是这个世界提前写好的情书。等待不是空白，等待是爱在练习。
content: 傍晚的时候，妈妈坐在窗前，手里拿着一只小小的铃铛。铃铛是铜色的，只有一颗樱桃那么大，系着一根淡粉色的丝带。妈妈把丝带绕在窗框上，打了一个蝴蝶结。然后她把手轻轻放在肚子上，小声说：「叮叮叮，唱给还没出生的小宝贝听吧。」
风正好路过窗台。它停下来——风没有脚，可它还是停了一下——想：小宝贝？什么小宝贝？风到处跑，什么都见过，可它没见过这个「小宝贝」。
风悄悄溜进屋子里。它看见一间小小的房间，墙刷成了鹅黄色，窗帘上绣着小云朵。房间中央摆着一只木头小床，小床里铺着软软的棉被，棉被上放着一只布偶兔子。小床空空的，可风觉得，那不是「空」，而是「满」——满满地装着等待。
风明白了。它从窗缝里钻出去，呼——地跑远了。它要去准备一份礼物。
风跑过一片麦田，金黄色的麦穗在夕阳里摇晃。风穿过麦穗，沙沙沙，沙沙沙。它把这声音轻轻卷起来，像卷一匹丝绸，卷啊卷，卷成一个小小的声音团子，揣在怀里。
风又跑过一条小河。河水在石头上溅起水花，叮咚，叮咚。风弯下腰，把水声也捡起来，和麦浪的声音放在一起。叮咚叮咚，沙沙沙沙，两种声音混在一起，像一首还没写完的歌。
风继续跑。它经过一棵老槐树，老槐树的叶子被风吹得哗啦哗啦响。风说：「老槐树，借我一点声音吧。」老槐树抖了抖身子，抖下最柔软的一片叶子，那片叶子打着旋儿落下来，发出簌簌的一声。风接住了。
风又路过一片荷塘。青蛙们正在开晚会，咕呱咕呱，此起彼伏。一只小青蛙鼓着腮帮子，用力叫了一声——咕——，那声音又圆又亮，像一颗绿色的珠子。风把它也收进了怀里。
天黑了。风抱着满满一怀的声音，跑回来了。它轻轻撞了一下窗框上的小铃铛。
铃铛响了。可这一次，铃声里不只有铃铛自己的声音。沙沙沙，是麦浪。叮咚叮咚，是小河。簌簌簌，是老槐树的落叶。咕——，是小青蛙。所有的声音都从铃铛里流淌出来，像一条温柔的小溪，流进那间鹅黄色的小房间。
妈妈靠在摇椅上，闭着眼睛，嘴角弯弯的。她的手还放在肚子上。小宝贝在温暖的地方，什么都看不见，可他听到了——不是用耳朵，是用一种比耳朵更古老的方式。他感觉到了世界在轻轻摇晃，像水波，像摇篮，像妈妈的心跳。
铃铛不响了。风悄悄地走了，去准备明天的声音团子。窗外的月亮照着小铃铛，铜色的铃铛在月光下闪着微微的光，像一颗小星星落在了窗台上。
妈妈在摇椅上睡着了。小房间里安安静静的。只有布偶兔子的眼睛亮晶晶的，好像在替所有人守望着——那还没来的小宝贝，和这已经准备好的世界。

title: The Owl Who Practiced Lullabies (Prenatal)
preview: In the old oak tree at the edge of the lane, there lived a small owl with a very plain name. Her name was Hattie, she was feathered and round, and she lived where the moss grew soft on the ground.
moral: The world begins singing to a child long before the child can hear. Every cricket's chirp and stream-bubble and owl's hoot is the earth's way of saying: we are ready for you. Love doesn't wait for a hello - it practices its song in advance.
content: In the old oak tree at the edge of the lane, there lived a small owl with a very plain name. Her name was Hattie, she was feathered and round, and she lived where the moss grew soft on the ground. Each night she would practice her hoo-hoo-hoo - hoo-hoo, hoo-hoo, hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo. But that wasn't the song she wanted to do.

For Hattie had heard (from the wind, who tells all to the birds and the bugs and the trees, short and tall) that someone was coming to the house down the bend - the little white house where the garden path ends. And this someone was small. So new and so small, not here yet at all!

'I must learn a lullaby,' Hattie declared. She puffed up her feathers and carefully stared at the moon and the stars and the whispering trees. 'A lullaby comes from the simplest of things.' So she tucked up her wings and she flew through the night to find all the sounds that were gentle and light.

First she flew to the meadow where crickets kept time - chirk-chirk, chirk-chirk, in a rhythm of rhyme. 'Oh crickets,' said Hattie, 'may I borrow your beat? I'm making a song for someone quite sweet.' The crickets looked up with their shiny black eyes and played her a rhythm, a gentle surprise. Chirk-chirk, chirk-chirk. Hattie nodded her head. 'That's the beginning!' she happily said.

Next she visited Bumbleby Pond, where the frogs sang songs from their lily-pad, moss-covered logs. A bullfrog named Milton, green-speckled and fat, cleared his wide throat and went: 'Rrribbit-rrr-AT!' 'Too loud,' Hattie whispered. 'Try softer, my friend.' So Milton tried again, softer this time, around the bend. 'Rrribbit... rrribbit... rrribbit-hush-hush.' 'Perfect!' said Hattie. 'Not too much, not too less, just.'

Then she stopped by the stream where the water ran clear and listened to bubbles go plip-plop, plip-phere. Plink-plank, plink-plank, kuplink-kuplank-kuplunk. 'That's the sound of a lullaby, chunk by chunk!' She gathered the water-sounds up in her head and mixed them with crickets and frogs, well-bred.

Back in her oak tree, she sorted it out - the chirk of the crickets, the plink of the trout (well, not a real trout, but the bubble-sounds, too), the rrribbit of Milton (soft, not loud, like new). She arranged them and hummed them and tried them again until her small feathers stood up like a pen.

Hoo-hoo, she began. Then: chirk-chirk, hoo-hoo. Plink-plank, rrribbit-hush. Hoo-hoo, hoo-hoo. It wasn't quite music, it wasn't quite words. It was the sound of the night when the dreaming occurs. It was the sound of the stream when the moonlight is silver. It was the sound of a mother's hum by the window-shiver.

Each night she practiced, and each night it grew softer and sweeter and truer and new. The wind carried pieces of it down the lane to the little white house with the red door and pane. And inside the house, in a room painted pale, a mama sat rocking, slow as a snail. She heard a faint hoo-hoo on the breeze and smiled at the moon and the old oak trees.
'Someone out there is singing to you,' she whispered so soft to the someone below, in the warm, safe dark. 'The world is practicing its song.'

For the world doesn't wait for a baby to arrive to start being gentle, to start being kind. The crickets keep time and the bullfrogs keep tune and the stream makes its music beneath the soft moon. And the owl in the oak tree practices each night a lullaby woven of meadow sounds and light.

Hoo-hoo, chirk-chirk. Plink-plank, hush-hush. Kuplink, kuplank, kuplunk. Rrribbit. Hoo. And somewhere, small and warm and not-quite-here, someone listened without ears to the song the world had been rehearsing all year.

title: 【胎教期】月亮妈妈的摇篮曲
preview: 月亮妈妈轻轻哼着歌，把柔柔的光洒在大地上。宝宝在妈妈肚子里，听着、听着，就安静下来了。
moral: 妈妈的声音是世界上最好听的声音，它像月光一样温柔，守护着宝宝长大。等待，也是爱的一部分。
content: 月亮妈妈挂在天空上，圆圆的，亮亮的，像一个大大的气球。她轻轻地哼着歌：「唔——唔——小宝宝，快快睡，妈妈在，不怕黑。」
风娃娃听见了，悄悄地吹过来，把歌声送到小树上。小树的叶子「沙沙沙」地响，好像在说：「真好听，真好听。」
月亮妈妈又哼着歌：「唔——唔——小星星，眨眼睛，妈妈的爱，亮晶晶。」星星们听见了，一闪一闪地眨着眼睛，好像在跳舞。
这时候，妈妈肚子里的小宝宝也听见了。他翻了个身，耳朵贴着小房子，听着月亮妈妈的歌。他的心「扑通扑通」跳着，像在打拍子。
妈妈把手放在肚子上，轻轻地说：「宝宝，你听，月亮妈妈在唱歌呢。她在等春天，等花开。妈妈也在等你，等你睁开眼睛，看看这个美丽的世界。」
月亮妈妈笑了，她的光变得更柔、更暖了，像一条软软的毯子，盖在大地上。宝宝打了个哈欠，闭上眼睛，在妈妈的歌声里，慢慢地睡着了。
后来啊，月亮妈妈每天都来唱歌。她唱呀唱，直到春天来了，花儿开了，宝宝也出生了。宝宝一听到妈妈的声音，就不哭了，因为他知道——那是世界上最温暖的声音。

title: The Little Lantern's Journey (Prenatal)
preview: In a quiet little town where the moon rose like a golden balloon, there lived a tiny lantern named Lumi. Lumi was no ordinary lantern—he was born from a firefly's wish and a mother's soft hum.
moral: Even a tiny light can find its way home with love, and every journey is easier when you listen to a loving voice.
content: In a quiet little town where the moon rose like a golden balloon, there lived a tiny lantern named Lumi. Lumi was no ordinary lantern—he was born from a firefly's wish and a mother's soft hum. Every night, he sat on a windowsill, glowing gently, waiting for someone to need him.

One evening, a little breeze whispered, 「Lumi, Lumi, a baby cloud has lost her way. She's floating all alone behind the hills. Can you help her find home?」 Lumi blinked his warm, golden light. 「I will try,」 he said softly, and off he drifted into the twilight.

He floated past a sleepy owl who hooted, 「Hoo, hoo, where are you going, little glow?」 Lumi answered, 「To find a lost cloud and bring her home.」 The owl nodded and said, 「Follow the sound of the lullaby—the river sings it every night.」

Lumi drifted down, down, down, to where the river hummed a gentle tune: 「Shhh, shhh, shhh.」 He saw a tiny white cloud huddled near a willow tree, shivering. 「Don't be scared,」 Lumi said. 「I'll guide you back. Just follow my light.」

Together they floated over fields of sleeping flowers—daisies dreaming of sunshine, tulips nodding in the breeze. The little cloud began to feel braver. 「Can you make your light blink like a star?」 she asked. Lumi blinked three times: blink, blink, blink. The cloud giggled, a soft pitter-patter of rain.

Soon they reached the sky's edge, where the moon hung low and golden. A big, puffy Mama Cloud was waiting with open arms. 「My little one!」 she said, wrapping the baby cloud in a hug. Then she turned to Lumi. 「Thank you, tiny lantern. Without you, she might have drifted forever.」

Lumi smiled and said, 「I just followed the lullaby. And the owl. And the river.」 Mama Cloud gave him a kiss of dew, and Lumi felt warm all over. He floated back to his windowsill, where the moon was now high and bright.

As he settled, a voice came from inside the house—a mother's voice, soft and low, humming the same lullaby the river sang. Lumi glowed a little brighter, knowing he was home. And he knew: even the smallest light can guide a lost heart home.
Goodnight, little Lumi. Goodnight, little one. May you always find your way home, just like the baby cloud. Sleep tight, and dream of gentle lights and loving voices.

title: 🔬科学故事（胎教期）冰底下那条红色的小溪
preview: 在很远很远的南极，有一座巨大的冰川。冰川的伤口里，悄悄流出一条红色的小溪，它来自一个从没见过阳光的世界。
moral: 即使在没有阳光的黑暗里，生命也会安静而顽强地生长；你也被同样的温柔与等待包围着。
content: 在地球最南端、白茫茫的南极大陆，有一座名叫泰勒的冰川。它安静地睡了很久很久。有一天，人们在冰川的边上发现了一件奇怪的事——冰层裂开了一道小小的缝，从缝里缓缓流出一条暗红色的小溪，像冰川在轻轻地流泪。
你别害怕，那不是真的血，也不是童话里的魔法。科学家爷爷用眼睛看、用仪器量，发现这条红色的小溪，其实是藏在冰底下很久很久的咸水。水里有好多好多的铁，就像妈妈厨房里的小铁勺。当这些水从冰底下冒出来、碰到空气，铁就慢慢地「生锈」了，变成了温柔的红色。
这条小溪的家，在冰川很深很深的肚子里。那里黑黑的，从来没有见过阳光，也没有风，安静得像宝宝在被窝里。可就在这样黑黑的地方，住着一群小小的、小小的生命——是肉眼几乎看不见的细菌和古菌。它们不用太阳公公，也能悄悄活着，用石头和铁当食物，安安静静地过着自己的日子。
科学家们觉得这真是一个奇迹：原来没有阳光的地方，也能有生命在轻轻地呼吸。他们还想到，在很远很远的太空里，木星和土星的那些冰月亮（叫木卫二、土卫二）的冰壳底下，也许也藏着这样的小海洋。也许，在那些我们看不见的黑暗里，也有温柔的生命在等待被发现。
所以呀，当宝宝你在妈妈肚子里，被温暖的羊水轻轻抱着、还没见到外面的阳光时，你并不孤单。在地球的南极，在冰月亮的海洋里，也有许多看不见的小生命，正和你一样，安安静静地等待着，等待有一天，去看见这个大大的、温柔的世界。

title: 🔬 Science Story (Prenatal) The Octopus with Eight Thinking Arms
preview: Deep in the blue ocean lives a clever octopus with eight arms — and each arm can think a little all by itself.
moral: Even the tiniest hidden parts of us work quietly to keep us safe and ready to wonder — just like you, growing in the calm dark.
content: Far below the waves, in the quiet blue of the ocean, lives one of the cleverest creatures of all — the octopus. She has a round soft head, two curious eyes, and eight long waving arms. Most animals keep their thinking in one brain, but the octopus is special: about two-thirds of her five hundred million tiny brain-cells live right inside her eight arms. Each arm can feel, hold, and even decide a little on its own.

Because of this, an octopus can do amazing things. She can slip a lid off a jar to find a tasty snack, sneak out of a puzzle of rocks, hide inside an empty coconut shell like a little traveling house, and even change her color to gently copy other sea animals. Some octopuses are so clever they learn to recognize the people who visit them, and say hello in their own quiet way.

Scientists wanted to know: what makes an octopus so smart? Not long ago, they found a tiny, secret trick hidden inside her cells. A special little piece of her ribbon-like genetic material (called ribosomal RNA) is shaped just a little differently from every other animal's. This small change helps her cells build their proteins very, very carefully — with almost no mistakes.

Why does that matter? Inside a clever animal, the brain-cells live a long, long time, and they can get messy if tiny proteins clump together. The octopus's little cellular trick keeps those clumps away, so her thinking stays clear and bright. It is like a tiny tidy-elf living in every cell, sweeping gently so her eight arms can keep learning and playing.

And here is the loveliest part: scientists hope that by learning the octopus's quiet trick, one day they might help keep human brains healthy too. So the next time you float peacefully in the warm dark, before you have met the sun, remember the clever octopus — proof that even the smallest, hidden parts of us are busy, gently, keeping us safe and ready to wonder.

title: 当当来我家
preview: 爸爸抱回来一个毛茸茸的小黑团子，他一身乌黑发亮的短毛，胸口的毛里却悄悄藏着一小撮白毛。这就是当当——一只中华田园小黑猫，从今天起，他住进了宝宝温暖的家。
moral: 调皮的当当虽然爱跑酷、爱闯小祸，可他最听爸爸妈妈的话——因为爸爸妈妈的爱，是这个家里最温暖的规矩。宝宝也要记得，听爸爸妈妈的话，最安全、最幸福。
content: 爸爸抱回来一个毛茸茸的小黑团子。他一身乌黑发亮的短毛，像擦得锃亮的小煤球；一双金黄色的眼睛圆溜溜的，最特别的是——胸口的毛里悄悄藏着一小撮白毛，像是偷偷点了一丁点儿牛奶。这就是当当，一只中华田园小黑猫。从今天起，他住进了宝宝温暖的家。

当当可调皮啦。他最爱在家里「跑酷」：从沙发嗖地跳上书架，再哧溜一下滑下猫爬架，爪子嗒嗒嗒、身子哧溜溜，把地板当成了他的小操场。他还最爱玩捉迷藏——嗒嗒嗒跑两步，哧溜一下就钻到床底下去，黑乎乎里缩成一小团，等爸爸妈妈弯下腰来找他，才探出小脑袋喵地叫一声；调皮的小家伙，藏得再隐蔽也舍不得真让爸爸妈妈着急。可只要爸爸妈妈伸手摸摸他的下巴，或轻轻揉一揉他的小肚皮，当当立刻眯起眼睛，喉咙里发出咕噜咕噜的声音——那是猫咪最开心的「小马达」在转。
家里还住着两只猫。姐姐小不点是一只雪白的猫，粉粉的小鼻子，安静又优雅，平时最爱在院子里慢慢散步，邻居见了都夸「这小白猫真乖」。哥哥八百是一只狸花猫，棕黑相间的斑纹，壮壮实实的，就是有点挑食，也怕生人、怕吵闹，一有动静就躲到床底下去；可他脾气特别温顺，被摸摸也会轻轻发呼噜。当当崇拜又心疼哥哥，总想带八百「见见世面」，八百只是慢吞吞地摇摇头。

爸爸妈妈立下了几条家规：听见名字要答应、要回家；出门要牵好小绳绳；不可以抓沙发；还要一起保护好宝宝——宝宝是家里最小、最宝贝的小成员，三只猫都要当他的小守护。别看当当爱闹，这几条他记在心里——因为爸爸妈妈的爱，是他最喜欢的安全感。爸爸常讲，中华田园猫是田野里最灵巧的小卫士，看粮仓、陪人家，一摸就咕噜；妈妈手机里存着大猫的照片——狮子、老虎，毛茸茸的大家伙亲戚。妈妈笑着戳戳当当的鼻尖：「你看，它们是你远方的大家伙亲戚。可不管多大，听爸爸妈妈的话，就不怕。」当当似懂非懂地点点头，把脸埋进爸爸的膝盖。
夜深了，窗外的风轻轻吹。墙角那个小小的水管洞里，悄悄探出一只灰扑扑的小老鼠——他只有一只耳朵，大家都叫他「一只耳」。一只耳眨巴着小眼睛，盯上了厨房里当当家的猫粮罐，咽了咽口水。当当的耳朵忽然动了动，金黄的眼睛在黑暗里亮了一下。不过别担心，有爸爸妈妈在，这个家永远暖暖的、安全的。要听爸爸妈妈的话，小冒险才能稳稳当当地开始——下一周，当当就要来保护他的家人和宝宝啦。

title: 当当大战一只耳
preview: 夜里，墙角传来窸窸窣窣的响声。一只灰溜溜的老鼠悄悄溜进了厨房，那是坏老鼠一只耳。
moral: 保护家人要勇敢，也要听爸爸妈妈的话——不随便追出门，才是真正聪明的小守护。
content: 宝宝呀，今天爸爸妈妈想给你讲讲当当第一次当小守护的故事。那天夜里，窗外的月亮像一枚小小的银币，家里静悄悄的，只有三只猫轻轻的呼噜声。
墙角传来窸窸窣窣的响动。一只灰溜溜的老鼠，左耳朵缺了一小块，大家都叫他一只耳，偷偷溜进厨房，想偷吃三只猫的猫粮，还想去吓唬乖巧的小不点。
当当最先听见了。他嗖地从猫爬架上滑下来，哧溜——稳稳落地，胸口那一小撮白毛都紧张地竖了起来。小不点轻轻喵了一声，躲到爸爸脚边；八百缩在床底下，只露出半张脸，尾巴尖微微发抖。
当当没有乱扑。他想起了爸爸妈妈立下的家规：听见名字要答应、要回家，出门要牵好小绳绳，不可以抓沙发，还要一起保护好宝宝。于是当当挡在猫粮盆前，尾巴一扇一扇，把一只耳慢慢赶向门口。
爸爸听见动静走过来，轻轻用储物箱把一只耳挡在门外，没有伤害他，只是温和地说：坏老鼠，回家去吧。一只耳吱吱叫着，从门缝溜走了。当当松了一口气，咕噜咕噜地蹭了蹭爸爸的手。
妈妈摸摸当当的下巴说：你今天很勇敢，也很聪明——没有追出门，是因为爸爸说过，夜里不能自己跑出去。当当点点头，把保护家人、听爸爸妈妈的话，都悄悄记在了心里。
宝宝呀，后来一只耳还远远地出现过两次，不过那是以后的故事了。这一夜，三只猫挤在一起，安安静静地睡着了，连梦里都暖暖的。

title: 爬山看星星
preview: 星期六的早晨，爸爸妈妈把宝宝放进软软的背包，带三只猫坐车去了郊外的小山。当当扒着车窗，第一次看见真正的蝴蝶。
moral: 出门要跟紧爸爸妈妈，听叮嘱才安全；当当也开始学着保护最小的你啦。
content: 宝宝呀，这个星期六，爸爸妈妈带你去爬山啦——当然，你还在妈妈肚子里，舒舒服服地坐在爸爸背的软背包里。三只猫也去了，当当兴奋得在猫包里转圈圈，尾巴尖一翘一翘。
山下的风带着青草和泥土的味道。车一停，当当就嗖地钻出来，哧溜一下跳上石头，金黄色的眼睛睁得圆圆的。一只白色的蝴蝶颤巍巍飞过，当当伸出爪子又缩回来——这是他第一次见到真的蝴蝶呢。
小不点慢悠悠跟在爸爸妈妈身后散步，粉鼻子一耸一耸，闻着野花。八百有点紧张，贴着爸爸的裤脚走，但风把一朵小黄花吹到他鼻尖，他居然没有躲，只是轻轻打了个喷嚏，耳朵抖了抖。
爬到半山腰，爸爸妈妈铺开野餐垫。当当在垫子上跑酷：从水壶跳到水果篮，再哧溜滑下爸爸的膝盖，嗒嗒嗒、哧溜，逗得小不点喵喵笑，连八百都眯起了眼睛。宝宝好像也开心，在肚子里轻轻动了动。
太阳落山，星星一颗一颗亮起来。爸爸说：天黑了，大家跟紧我的手电光，不可以乱跑。当当记住了家规，乖乖走在爸爸妈妈脚边，没有追着萤火虫往林子深处钻。
下山的路，当当一直护着爸爸背上的背包——那里有宝宝呀。他迈着小碎步，胸口那撮白毛在星光下微微发亮。妈妈悄悄说：你看，当当真的在学怎么保护宝宝了。
宝宝呀，那只白蝴蝶，后来飞去了很远很远的地方。但每当星星亮起来，当当就会抬头看一眼，好像在跟你说：放心，我和哥哥姐姐，都会保护好你。

title: 老钟楼的秘密
preview: 古镇的石板路被太阳晒得暖暖的。当当在一座老钟楼下，把一块刻着字的石碑当成了喵喵碑，还帮邻居老奶奶捡回了滚落的毛线球。
moral: 帮助别人很快乐，兄弟姐妹一起帮忙，事情就会变得又暖又简单。
content: 宝宝呀，这周爸爸妈妈带三只猫去了有老钟楼的小镇。那里的房子都有翘翘的屋檐，风铃叮叮当当，像在唱一支很老很老的歌。
老钟楼前立着一块石碑，上面刻着弯弯曲曲的字。当当歪着脑袋看了半天，认定那是专给猫看的喵喵碑，还郑重地用脑袋蹭了蹭，表示自己看懂了。小不点在一旁抿着嘴笑，八百则抬头数钟楼上的小窗户，一、二、三……数到一半就忘了。
这时，邻居老奶奶的毛线球从篮子里滚出来，咕噜咕噜滚下台阶。老奶奶弯不下腰，有点着急。当当嗖地追上去，用爪子轻轻按住毛线球；八百慢慢挪过来，用鼻子把毛线球推回老奶奶脚边。
老奶奶笑得眼角皱成花：谢谢你们呀，小猫咪。小不点乖巧地蹭了蹭她的拐杖，像在说不用谢。三只猫排成一队，把毛线球一颗一颗护送回篮子，一步也不乱，尾巴尖都骄傲地翘着。
回家的巷口，当当忽然竖起耳朵——墙角黑影一闪，是一只耳！他远远探了下头，看见三只猫紧紧挨着爸爸妈妈，便吱吱一声，又缩了回去。当当没有追，他记得家规：听见名字要答应，但夜里不能自己跑出去。
晚上，爸爸给肚里的你讲钟楼的故事：很多很多年前，也有一只小黑猫，守着镇上的孩子。当当趴在爸爸脚边，咕噜咕噜，好像听懂了——原来守护这件事，是一代一代传下来的。
宝宝呀，帮助别人的快乐，就像钟楼的钟声，会一声一声，飘得很远很远。

title: 龙宫的珍珠
preview: 午后，当当趴在鱼缸边打了个哈欠，啪嗒——他梦见自己掉进了蓝幽幽的龙宫，遇见一条丢了珍珠的小龙。
moral: 把喜欢的东西分给别人，心里装着别人，就是最温柔的分享；也要记得听爸爸妈妈的话哦。
content: 宝宝呀，这周的故事发生在当当的午睡梦里。午后的阳光暖暖的，当当趴在鱼缸边，尾巴尖一翘一翘，打了个长长的哈欠——啪嗒，他掉进了一个蓝幽幽、亮晶晶的地方。
那是龙宫。水草像丝绸一样飘，小鱼排着队吐泡泡。一条胖乎乎的小龙着急地游来游去：我的珍珠不见了！没有珍珠，龙宫的灯就不亮了。当当拍拍胸脯：别急，我帮你找！
他们钻过珊瑚桥，扒开贝壳堆，还问了慢吞吞的老海龟。最后，在一只贪睡的大贝壳里，当当用爪子轻轻一拨——噗，珍珠滚了出来，圆溜溜、亮闪闪，像一颗小小的月亮。
小龙把珍珠嵌回龙宫顶上，哗，整个龙宫都亮了。他摘下一片会发光的鳞片送给当当：这是谢礼，也请你分给真正需要的小朋友。当当想了想，说：那我要送给家里最小的宝宝。
梦忽然轻轻地散了。当当睁开眼，发现自己还趴在鱼缸边，爪子里抱着的，是爸爸钥匙串上那颗圆圆的白纽扣——他把它当成了龙宫的珍珠。他嗖地跑到爸爸背包旁，把纽扣轻轻放在你（宝宝）的位置边。
爸爸看见了，蹲下来摸摸当当：这是要给宝宝的礼物呀？当当咕噜咕噜点头。妈妈笑着说：分享，就是心里装着别人；当当这么小，就学会啦。她还轻轻补了一句：不过呀，想把这么宝贝的东西送给宝宝，要先问过爸爸妈妈哦——当当记住了，把听爸爸妈妈的话，也悄悄收进了心里。
宝宝呀，龙宫也许是梦，但当当想给你的那颗珍珠，是真的。等你来了，他一定第一个捧到你面前。

title: 智斗格格巫
preview: 一个爱搞怪的卡通巫师格格巫，想用怪声音引走宝宝的笑声。三只猫开动脑筋，一家人合作，把宝宝稳稳护在了中间。
moral: 不跟陌生人走，听爸爸妈妈的话；一家人齐心协力，就能保护好最重要的你。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，家里来了一位不速之客——格格巫。他不是真巫师，是个爱搞怪的卡通家伙，戴着尖帽子，想用叽里咕噜的怪声音，把你的笑声引走，装进他的小布袋里。
当当最先听见那怪声音，耳朵啪地竖起来。他想起家规里最重要的一条：保护好宝宝。于是当当没有冲出去，而是嗖地跑到爸爸背包旁，把小小的身子挡在你前面，胸口那撮白毛都绷得紧紧的。
小不点轻手轻脚走到妈妈怀里，用软软的毛蹭着妈妈，让妈妈把宝宝护得更紧；八百虽然怕生，也慢慢挪到门边，用壮实的身子堵住门口，呼噜呼噜给自己壮胆，尾巴尖微微发抖却一步不退。
格格巫在窗外晃着布袋喊：小猫咪，出来玩呀，我带你去看好玩的！当当记着爸爸的话：不跟陌生人走。他甩甩尾巴，和哥哥姐姐一起，把格格巫的怪声音用喵喵歌盖了过去——咕噜咕噜、喵呜喵呜，家里暖暖的，一点也不怕。
爸爸走过去，把窗帘拉上，温和地说：格格巫，我们家不跟不认识的人走哦。格格巫撇撇嘴，尖帽子一歪，咕噜滚下了台阶。墙角那只耳探了下头，看见三只猫这么齐心，也吱吱一声溜走了——这下，两只捣蛋鬼都老实了。
夜里，三只猫挤在宝宝背包旁边，像三个小小的守卫。妈妈轻轻说：从今天起，你们就是宝宝的守护队啦。当当把胸口那撮白毛贴着背包，咕噜咕噜：放心，我们一直都在。
宝宝呀，外面的世界很大，也会有奇怪的声音。但只要你听见爸爸妈妈和我们三只猫的咕噜声，就知道——你被好好地爱着，也被好好地守护着。

title: 狸花阿姨来做客
preview: 小区里的狸花阿姨来家里做客，偷瞄当当的小鱼干，却在家规面前乖乖坐好；夜里一只耳又来捣乱，狸花阿姨和当当一起把它请了出去。
moral: 好东西要分享，也要看好自己的小零食；听爸爸妈妈的话，家里每个人都来保护宝宝。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，咱们家来了一位特别的客人——狸花阿姨。她是小区里自由串门的美食家猫咪，棕黑相间的花纹，尾巴粗粗长长，走路优雅得像位长辈。她最爱打听小区里的新鲜八卦，鼻子比谁都灵，一闻见好吃的就迈不动腿。
狸花阿姨是来和当当他们吃饭的。当当把自己的小鱼干摆得整整齐齐，狸花阿姨坐在一边，眼睛直勾勾盯着盘子，尾巴尖悄悄往碗边探——可是她记得这是别人家，乖乖蹲在桌边，只偷偷咽了咽口水。当当看见了，叼起一块小鱼干，轻轻推到她面前：阿姨，这块给你。狸花阿姨愣了愣，慢慢吃起来，眼睛弯成了月牙。
饭后，狸花阿姨趴在窗台晒太阳，给当当讲小区里发生的趣事：哪只麻雀当了妈妈，哪朵月季今年开得最早。小不点挨着她，把打结的白毛伸过去，狸花阿姨用爪子轻轻理了理，像位温柔的长辈。八百难得没躲起来，也蜷在旁边打起了呼噜。
天黑了，当当正趴在宝宝背包边陪睡。墙角水管洞里，那只耳又探出了头——它闻着晚饭的香味，想溜进来偷剩下的小鱼干。狸花阿姨耳朵一竖，悄无声息地挪到洞边，猛地一伸爪，把一只耳吓得嗷一声缩了回去。当当也竖起胸口那撮白毛，挡在宝宝前面：不许碰我们的家！
爸爸听见动静走过来，轻轻把洞口用储物箱挡住，温和地说：一只耳，别人家的东西不能拿哦。狸花阿姨甩甩尾巴：小家伙，下次再来，阿姨请你吃正经猫草。一只耳在箱外吱吱两声，灰溜溜溜走了。这一晚，家里又恢复了暖暖的安静。
宝宝呀，狸花阿姨来的这一天，当当学会了两件事：好东西要分给客人，自己的小零食也要看牢；更重要的是，家里每一位成员，连来做客的阿姨，都会一起把宝宝护在中间。
夜深了，三只猫和狸花阿姨挤在宝宝背包旁。当当把胸口那撮白毛贴着背包，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，你看，我们的家越来越大，爱也越来越多啦。

title: 南京紫金山·南南带队爬山
preview: 当当一家来到南京紫金山，野猪南南当起山地导游，带大家摘野酸枣、看山间风景；一只耳偷偷跟来想偷特产，被南南和当当一起找了回来。
moral: 出门要跟紧爸爸妈妈，听叮嘱才安全；外面的世界很大很美，一双眼睛慢慢看，两只小手紧紧牵。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，咱们家出门旅行啦！爸爸妈妈带着三只猫，坐上高铁，去了南京的紫金山。山脚下，一位圆滚滚的小伙伴早就等着了——野猪南南。他棕褐色的短硬毛，头顶一撮浅棕色软绒毛，小獠牙软软的，跑起来像一阵小旋风，是这座山的专属导游。
南南可兴奋了，领着大家沿小路往上走，一边指一边讲：这是野酸枣树，那是隐秘的小瀑布，远处那个观景台能看见整座南京城。当当第一次闻到山里的风，有青草和泥土的味道，他忍住乱跑的冲动，紧紧跟在爸爸手边——妈妈说过，山里不能自己乱闯。
半山腰，南南从背包里掏出野酸枣，分给每只猫：尝尝，山里的甜！当当咬了一口，酸得耳朵一抖，又慢慢品出回甘，咯咯笑起来。小不点优雅地小口吃着；八百平时挑食，这回竟也啃了酸枣，南南拍拍他壮实的背：兄弟，山里的饭，香吧？
忽然，当当的耳朵动了动——他看见岩缝里一截灰尾巴一闪。是一只耳！它偷偷跟来了南京，正想把南南背包里的南京特产往自己破布口袋里塞。南南眯起眼：嘿，小偷还跟到山上来了？
南南带着当当，顺着脚印追过去。当当没有莽撞扑，而是想起家规：不自己乱跑、听爸爸妈妈的话。他喵呜一声唤来爸爸，爸爸和南南一起，把一只耳堵在了石头后面。一只耳举着小爪子：我、我就闻闻……南南把特产收好，递给它一块酸枣：想吃自己摘去，别动别人的。
下山时，夕阳把紫金山染成橘红色。当当走在爸爸背包旁，那里有宝宝；南南扛着满满一包南京特产，说要寄给当当当零食。宝宝呀，这一天，当当看见了比家里大得多的世界，也记住了：走得再远，也要跟紧爸爸妈妈的手。
夜里住民宿，三只猫挤在宝宝背包边。当当把胸口那撮白毛贴着背包，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，等你也出来了，爸爸一定带你来看真的山。南南在门外打了个哈欠：下次，去我老家吃桂花糕！

title: 茅山遇修猴子
preview: 一家人去常州近郊的仙山茅山，山顶老桃树下遇见会温和小法术的修猴子：教当当让桃叶轻轻飘、和南南开玩笑、把格格巫看呆的彩虹；结尾修猴子丢下一句「老友粉在广西等你们」，为日后的广西之旅埋下伏笔。整篇是当当讲给肚里还没来的宝宝听的冒险。
moral: 奇妙的朋友要用温柔的方式相处；学到的本事要用来制造快乐，不用来捣乱。（哥哥讲给弟弟听的故事，也是守护的一种方式。）
content: 宝宝呀，今天哥哥当当给你讲个他去过的地方——茅山。你还没来的时候，咱们一家人去爬过茅山呢，那是离常州不远的一座仙山，道观藏在云雾里。
山顶道观旁的老桃树下，坐着一位金红色的小猴子，身披迷你青色小道袍，腰间挂着装满鲜果的小布袋——他就是修猴子。别看他调皮，可是个会温和小法术的修道者。
修猴子一见当当，眼睛亮了：小黑猫，来，我教你个好玩的！他掐了个诀，一片桃叶轻轻飘起来，在当当鼻尖打了个转，又稳稳落回手心。当当看得睁圆了金黄的眼睛，胸口那撮白毛都跟着翘了翘。修猴子说：这法术不伤人，只用来制造快乐。
正说着，南南哼哧哼哧爬上山来，修猴子嘻嘻一笑，把南南的背包悄悄隐了身。南南急得满山找：我特产呢我特产呢！修猴子躲在树后偷笑，最后才把背包变回来，还附赠一颗鲜桃。南南佯装生气，实则乐呵呵：你这调皮猴子！
爸爸蹲下来，让当当也试试。当当学着修猴子的样子，用小爪子轻轻一托，一片落叶真的慢慢飘了起来——虽然只飘了半寸就掉下，但全家都鼓起掌来。修猴子挠挠头：不错不错，有悟性！小不点用白毛蹭了蹭当当：弟弟，你也会魔法啦。
忽然，远处的林子传来叽里咕噜的怪响——是格格巫！修猴子眉头一皱，掐诀喷出一小朵云，轻轻把格格巫的怪声音盖了过去；又变出一道小彩虹，横在格格巫面前。格格巫看呆了，忘了捣乱，尖帽子一歪坐下来看彩虹。
修猴子还把一颗桃子塞给当当：常来玩，下次教你唤云朵。当当把这句话悄悄记在心里——真正的本事，不是用来吓人，而是用来让大家笑的。
最妙的是，修猴子在桃树上晃着腿，远远丢下一句：老友粉在广西等你们哦！所以呀，等宝宝你来了，哥哥就带你去广西，看那位长鼻子的大象朋友。
夜里，当当趴在宝宝的小床边，把这故事轻轻讲给你听。你咗咗嘴，好像也喜欢。小不点用白毛蹭蹭当当：弟弟，你又交到奇妙的朋友啦。八百难得没躲，也挨过来，用壮实的身子挡在床角。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，世界上有好多奇妙的朋友，等你来了，当当带你一个一个去认识。

title: 广西遇老友粉
preview: 一家去广西雨林，大象老友粉当向导：长鼻子摘高处的芒果、吸水浇花，还讲雨林里鹦鹉和小猴子的故事。中午吃热乎乎的老友粉，老友粉塞给当当一块芒果干带给宝宝。
moral: 外面的世界很大很美，一双眼睛慢慢看，两只小手紧紧牵——跟紧爸爸妈妈，走到哪儿都安心。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，咱们家出门去广西啦！你还记得吗，修猴子在茅山喊过：『老友粉在广西等你们哦！』这回，我们真的去找他了。
广西的雨林绿得发亮。一棵大树下，站着一头圆滚滚的小象——他就是老友粉。长长的鼻子一甩一甩，像一条温柔的小蛇。
老友粉可会帮忙啦。高高的芒果挂在枝头，他伸长鼻子，『卷——』轻轻一勾，果子就落进当当怀里。椰子太硬？他的鼻子一托一举，『咚』，稳稳放到地上。
渴了，老友粉用鼻子吸饱清清的水，再『噗』地喷成小水雾，给花儿洗个凉凉的澡。当当看得眼睛都圆了，胸口白毛一翘一翘。
雨林里还有会说话的鹦鹉，叽叽喳喳讲着彩色的故事；小猴子在藤上荡来荡去，吱吱笑。老友粉说：这里的朋友，都爱轻轻的、慢慢的日子。
中午，一家人吃广西的老友粉。热乎乎的汤，酸酸香香的，当当舔了一小口，耳朵抖了抖：好特别呀！老友粉从背包里掏出一块芒果干，塞给当当：带回去给宝宝尝尝。
下山时，当当紧紧挨着爸爸的手。妈妈说过，外面的世界很大，要跟紧爸爸妈妈。当当现在懂了——走得再远，宝宝的样子就在心里。
一只耳这次没跟来，老友粉说：这儿山高林密，小老鼠可不敢来。当当松了口气，趴在爸爸背包边（那里有宝宝的小桃木护身）。
夜里住吊脚楼。三只猫守在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，广西的芒果可甜啦，等你来了，爸爸一定带你来。
老友粉在远处甩了甩长鼻子，哞——地轻声应了一句。雨林的风，把这句问候，吹得好远好远。

title: 西太湖荷叶漂流
preview: 不用出远门，就在常州的西太湖，青蛙小西带当当坐荷叶船漂流：拨水叮咚、闻荷花、采莲蓬。一只耳想偷小鱼干，被小西一口水柱喷回洞里。
moral: 家门口也有好风景，和小伙伴慢慢玩；天黑不往深处跑，听爸爸妈妈的招呼就回家。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周不用出远门。咱们就在常州的西太湖，和青蛙小西一起玩！
小西是只翠绿翠绿的小青蛙，肚皮白白的，最爱晒太阳，也最爱说话——话痨得很。他一见到当当就呱呱叫：来来来，我带你坐荷叶船！
湖面荷叶田田，像撑开的一把把小绿伞。当当蹦上最大那片荷叶，『晃悠——』荷叶轻轻一沉又弹起来，像坐上了软软的小船。
小西在前头领路，扑通、扑通，溅起亮亮的水珠。当当学着用爪子拨水，叮咚、叮咚，湖水唱起了歌。
荷花开得粉粉的。小西说：这是西太湖的夏天。当当凑近闻了闻，一股清清淡淡的香，忍不住『阿嚏』打了个小喷嚏，逗得小西呱呱笑。
采莲蓬啦！小西递给当当一颗嫩绿的莲子，当当咬开，苦苦的又回甘。小不点优雅地小口吃着；八百平时不爱水，这回也探出爪子，轻轻碰了碰荷叶尖上的水珠。
忽然，当当瞥见岸边草丛一截灰尾巴——一只耳又来啦！它想偷小西晒在石头上的小鱼干。小西鼓起腮帮子，『噗！』一口水柱射过去，正中小老鼠的鼻尖。一只耳『吱——』地缩回洞里，再不敢露头。
傍晚，湖面染成橘红色。爸爸妈妈在岸边喊：当当，回家啦，天黑不往深处跑哦。当当喵呜一声，跟着小西游回岸边，紧挨着妈妈。
小西蹲在石头上挥爪：下次再来，我教你捉萤火虫！当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小车，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，西太湖的风，是荷叶味的哟。
夜里的湖安静下来，只有青蛙的呱呱，一声一声，像在给小宝宝唱晚安。

title: 小狗钱包回爸爸老家
preview: 雪纳瑞小狗钱包带当当回爸爸老家的山野徒步。钱包最会追踪脚印：野兔的、山鸡的，他都认得。一只耳又跟来偷特产，被钱包循着脚印找回，还请它吃了块烤红薯。
moral: 看不见的路，脚印会告诉你；跟紧爸爸妈妈的手，就是跟着最稳的『脚印』走。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，咱们去爸爸的老家山野，是一只特别的朋友带路的——小狗钱包。
钱包可不是普通小狗，他是一只雪纳瑞！黑黑的卷毛，小胡子翘翘的，背着一个帆布小包，每天早上晨跑。他最厉害的本领，是追踪脚印。
山野里风凉凉的。钱包低着鼻子，这儿闻闻、那儿嗅嗅：『当当，你瞧，这是野兔的脚印，小小的、分两半；那是山鸡的，带小爪尖。』当当跟在后面，把每道脚印都记在心里。
爬到半山，钱包从包里掏出烤红薯，香喷喷的。当当咬了一口，甜甜的、软软的。小不点优雅地小口吃；八百难得没躲，也挨过来，钱包拍拍他：兄弟，山里的饭，香吧？
忽然，钱包的耳朵竖起来：不对，有别人的脚印混进来了——一只耳！它又跟来啦，正往破布口袋里塞钱包准备的特产。
钱包不慌不忙：看我的。他顺着脚印，一步一步追过去，当当也喵呜唤来爸爸。石头后面，一只耳举着小爪子：我就闻闻……钱包用鼻子一拱，把特产收好，递给它一块红薯：想吃自己找去，别动别人的。
下山时，夕阳把山染成金红色。钱包说：记住哦，看不见的路，脚印会告诉你。当当把这句话，悄悄记在心里——跟紧爸爸妈妈，也是跟着最稳的『脚印』。
一只耳这回没被赶跑，而是被请去吃了一口正经零食。它啃着红薯，小眼睛眨了眨，好像第一次觉得：被温柔对待，比偷东西暖和。
夜里住山里小院。三只猫挤在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，钱包叔叔的鼻子可灵啦，以后迷路也不怕。
远处山风轻轻吹，带着红薯的甜香。宝宝呀，这世上好多朋友，都用自己特别的样子，保护着咱们。

title: 卡莎的定远庙会
preview: 回妈妈的老家安徽定远，民俗探索家卡莎带当当逛古镇庙会：红灯笼、糖画、石臼捶糍粑，还爬上老屋屋顶看小镇。妈妈买了一瓶小磨香油，说这是外婆家的味道。
moral: 记住老家，就记住了根；好多温柔的风景和手艺，都是长辈一点点留给我们的。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，咱们回妈妈的老家——安徽定远！带路的是一位飞檐走壁的朋友，叫卡莎。
卡莎是一只雪白长毛的猫，蓝莹莹的眼睛，身手轻得像片云。她是民俗探索家，最爱讲老房子的飞檐和那些老故事。
古镇的青石板路弯弯曲曲。庙会正热闹：红红的灯笼挂成一排，糖画师傅手腕一转，一条小金龙就出来了；糍粑在石臼里被捶得咚咚响，香喷喷的。
卡莎带当当爬上老屋的屋顶。当当第一次从高处看小镇——灰瓦一片片，像鱼鳞；炊烟一缕缕，慢慢飘上天空。卡莎说：这是妈妈小时候看过的风景。
剪纸摊前，老奶奶手一剪一剪，窗花就开了：有胖娃娃，有喜鹊登梅。当当看得入神，胸口白毛都跟着轻轻抖。卡莎悄悄说：每张红纸里，都藏着一句祝福。
妈妈在摊位前买了一小瓶小磨香油，笑着说：这是外婆家的味道。当当这才知道，妈妈原来也是从这样一个有灯笼、有炊烟的小镇出来的。
一只耳这回没来——定远的巷子太绕，它怕迷路。当当松了口气，乖乖跟在妈妈手边，听卡莎讲每一块老砖的故事。
傍晚，卡莎在屋顶上打了个滚，白毛沾了点夕阳的金。她甩甩尾巴：当当，记住老家，就记住了根。当当把这句话，轻轻贴进心里。
夜里住妈妈老家的老屋。三只猫守在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，你妈妈的老家，有红灯笼，有糍粑香，还有卡莎这样飞檐走壁的朋友。
窗外的定远安静下来，只有远处隐隐的狗吠，和妈妈轻轻哼起的家乡小调。

title: 小狗芒果的摇滚连线
preview: 不出门也认识了远方的朋友——东北沈阳的摇滚小狗芒果。视频电话里，他抱着迷你木吉他教当当唱摇滚儿歌；屏幕那头飘着雪，还举起了冻梨和烤冷面。
moral: 朋友不一定在身边，视频里也能一起唱歌、一起笑；『云』也能把好朋友连在一起。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周咱们不出门，却认识了一位很远很远的朋友——小狗芒果，住在东北的沈阳。
芒果是一只毛茸茸的小狗，最爱摇滚。他给当当打了个视频电话：屏幕一亮，他就抱着一把迷你小木吉他，汪汪地说：当当，我教你唱摇滚儿歌！
当当把小肉垫按在屏幕上，咯咯笑。芒果拨动琴弦，叮叮咚咚，唱道：『摇啊摇，小猫咪，夜晚不害怕——』当当跟着哼，喵呜喵呜，虽然跑调，可开心极了。
屏幕里，沈阳正下着雪。芒果推开窗户，雪花呼呼飘，松树戴上了白帽子。他说：看，这是东北的冬天！还举起冻梨和烤冷面：这个冰冰凉，这个香喷喷，等你去尝。
小不点也凑过来看，蓝眼睛映着雪花；八百难得没躲镜头，歪着脑袋听吉他。三只猫排成一排，跟着芒果的节拍，尾巴一摆一摆。
芒果说：朋友不一定在身边，视频里也能一起唱歌、一起笑。当当把这句话记下来——原来『云』也能把好朋友连在一起。
一只耳在墙角偷看，看见当当对着屏幕又唱又跳，觉得没意思，嗖地溜了。这回它没来捣乱，倒是省了事。
唱累了，芒果在屏幕那头打了个哈欠：当当，下次我教你弹真的吉他！当当用爪子碰了碰屏幕，像在说再见。
夜里，三只猫守在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，沈阳的雪好白，芒果的歌好吵好欢乐——等你来了，咱们也视频认识远方的朋友。
窗外的常州没有雪，可当当觉得，心里好像也落了小小的、快乐的雪花。

title: 八百不挑食了
preview: 哥哥八百终于不挑食啦！妈妈做小笼包和萝卜干，八百第一次啊呜一口，鲜得眼睛发亮。一只耳又来偷小笼，被八百用鼻子拱出门外——这回八百可勇敢了。
moral: 长大就是这样：一点点试，一点点勇敢，原来的害怕，就慢慢变成了喜欢。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，咱们家发生了一件大事——哥哥八百，不挑食啦！
你还记得吗？从前八百可挑了：青菜不吃，鱼不吃，闻到没见过的东西就扭头。去紫金山那回，他才第一次啃了野酸枣；去山野，才第一次吃烤红薯。
这周，妈妈在厨房做常州小吃：小笼包，白白胖胖；萝卜干，脆脆香香。八百蹲在门口，鼻子一动一动，居然没躲。
爸爸笑着递给他一小块小笼包皮：尝尝？八百犹豫了一下，啊呜一口——汤汁在嘴里爆开，鲜鲜的！他眼睛亮了，又伸出爪子要。
当当在旁边啪嗒啪嗒跑酷庆祝，小不点用白毛蹭蹭八百：哥哥，你长大啦。八百难得地昂了昂头，壮实的身子挺得直直的。
忽然，墙角一闪——一只耳又来啦！它想偷笼屉里的小笼包。八百这回不躲了，鼻子一拱，『呼』地把一只耳拱出了厨房门，还用身子堵住门口，像ep06那样神气。
一只耳举着小爪子：我就闻闻……八百哼了一声，从自己那份里推了一小块皮过去：吃这个，别动宝宝的。一只耳啃着，小眼睛又眨了眨——被温柔对待，真的比偷东西暖和。
晚饭，全家人一起吃。八百把每样都尝了点，连萝卜干都嘎吱嘎吱嚼得欢。妈妈摸摸他的头：我们八百，真的长大了。
夜里，三只猫守在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，哥哥八百从挑食小猫，变成勇敢又不挑嘴的大猫啦。
宝宝呀，长大就是这样：一点点试，一点点勇敢，原来的害怕，就慢慢变成了喜欢。

title: 格格巫的新伪装
preview: 爱搞怪的格格巫换上新模样——扮成送货猫，想骗走宝宝的笑声；一只耳这回跟他搭了伙。当当记着『不跟陌生人走』，三只猫齐齐护成一圈，把两条反派线轻轻请了回去。
moral: 坏人不可怕，记住爸爸妈妈的话、不跟陌生人走，家就稳稳的；温柔的对待，有时也能让捣乱的人软下来。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，那个爱搞怪的格格巫，又来了。这回，他还换了新模样。
他戴上一顶圆圆的小帽子，背个快递包，在窗外尖着嗓子喊：送零食啦——送给宝宝的小笑声！他想把宝宝的笑声，骗进他的小布袋里。
一只耳这回跟他搭了伙。小老鼠躲在格格巫背后，小声说：我帮你望风。两只反派，凑在了一起。
当当第一个听见。他没有冲出去——他记着家规：不跟陌生人走。他挡在宝宝小床前，胸口白毛竖得直直的。
小不点钻进妈妈怀里，守着还没来的宝宝；八百用壮实身子堵住门口，像ep06、ep15那样。三只猫，又齐齐护成了一个圈。
格格巫晃着布袋：来嘛，跟我去看好玩的。当当喵呜一声：妈妈说，不跟不认识的人走！爸爸走过来，轻轻拉上窗帘：小朋友，送货请走正门哦。
一只耳在旁边看看当当，又看看自己手里那块八百给的零食，忽然不想帮格格巫了。它悄悄退到洞边，吱吱两声，像是跟反派说了再见。
格格巫的帽子一歪——他看见连一只耳都走了，自己孤零零的。爸爸递过一块小桃饼（就是宝宝那种桃木护身旁的甜点）：吃口正经的，别老想着骗笑声。格格巫愣了愣，啃了一口，尖帽子慢慢垂下来。
这回，两条反派线并成了一条，又被轻轻地、温柔地请走了。当当明白：坏人不可怕，记住爸爸妈妈的话，家就稳稳的。
夜里，三只猫守在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，不管谁来敲门，当当都守着你，不跟陌生人走。

title: 大金毛的楼上派对
preview: 楼上住的大金毛请当当去做客。金毛哥哥脾气特别温和，给当当铺软垫、倒零食，静静地陪着。当当第一次自己去朋友家，安安心心玩了一下午。
moral: 好邻居就像另一份家人；有礼貌地去做客，世界会多一个温柔的角落。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，咱们家楼上住的大金毛，请当当去做客啦！
大金毛是一只金黄色的大家伙，毛软软的，个子比当当高好几个头，可脾气特别温和。他敲敲门：小黑猫，上来玩呀？
当当有点紧张——他还从没自己上过别人家。妈妈帮他把小绳绳系好：去吧，记得有礼貌。当当嗒嗒嗒跑上楼，尾巴尖有点抖。
大金毛的家好暖。他给当当铺了软软的垫子，倒出一小碗猫零食：尝尝？当当小心地咬了一口，眼睛弯成月牙。
大金毛不吵不闹，就静静地陪着。当当渐渐放松，居然在垫子上打了个滚，咕噜咕噜转起小马达。大金毛笑了：小家伙，你真可爱。
窗台上晒太阳，大金毛讲楼上的风景：哪只鸽子常来，哪朵云最好看。当当把胸口白毛贴着窗，金黄的眼睛映着夕阳，安安静静的。
一只耳这回没敢上楼——它怕大金毛的大爪子。当当松了口气，安心做客。
回家时，大金毛送到门口：常来玩呀。当当喵呜一声，蹭了蹭他那金灿灿的腿。这是当当第一次，自己去朋友家做客。
夜里，三只猫守在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，楼上的金毛哥哥好温柔。以后你也认得他，他是咱家的好邻居。
楼上隐隐传来大金毛轻轻的呼噜，和楼下的当当，一上一下，像在合奏一首安眠的小曲。

title: 当当的小法术升级
preview: 修猴子从广西打来视频电话，教当当的『轻轻飘叶』升级了——这次能飘一尺高！当当把小叶子飘到宝宝鼻尖逗得宝宝在梦里弯了弯嘴角。奇妙朋友这一段，先讲到这儿。
moral: 学到的本事，要用来制造快乐；从守护一个背包，到守护还没来的你，当当一点点，在长大。
content: 宝宝呀，这一周，当当的小法术，升级啦！你还记得吗，在茅山，修猴子教过他『轻轻飘叶』——那时只能飘半寸就掉。
修猴子从广西给当当打了个视频电话（老友粉帮他连的线）。他掐了个诀，一片桃叶慢慢飘起来：当当，再试试？
当当学爸爸的样子，用小爪子轻轻一托——呼，叶子真的飘起来，飘了一尺高，才慢慢落下！全家都鼓起掌来，小不点蹭蹭他：弟弟，你会魔法啦。
当当想：这法术，要用来做什么呢？他跑到宝宝小床边，用爪子一托——一片小叶子，轻轻飘到宝宝的小床边，转了个圈，又落回手心。
宝宝在梦里弯了弯小嘴角（虽然还没来，可好像听见了）。当当胸口白毛翘得高高的：宝宝，你看，当当会逗你笑啦！
修猴子在屏幕那头挠挠头：不错不错，有悟性！记住哦，法术不伤人，只用来制造快乐。当当用力点头。
一只耳在墙角看了一会儿，看见当当用叶子逗得宝宝笑，也悄悄咧了咧嘴——它好像，也开始喜欢看这个家暖暖的样子了。
夜里，三只猫守在宝宝的小床边。当当把胸口白毛贴着宝宝的小床，咕噜咕噜：宝宝，从守护『背包』到守护你，从飘半寸到飘一尺，当当一点点，在长大。
修猴子在远方甩了甩桃枝，老友粉甩了甩长鼻子，芒果在沈阳拨了下吉他——好多好朋友，都在不同的地方，轻轻想着这个小宝宝。
宝宝呀，这一阶段的奇妙朋友，先讲到这儿。往后的日子，还有更多山水、更多温柔的相遇，等你，和当当，一起慢慢走。

title: 屋檐下的小燕子
preview: 宝宝呀，上一周，当当学会了让小叶子飘起来一尺高，把你逗得咯咯笑。这一周，他遇上了一件更要紧的事——院子的草丛里，有个小小的声音在唧唧唧地哭。
moral: 帮忙是件很好的事，可帮忙之前，要先听爸爸妈妈的话：不乱碰、先叫大人，才是真的帮到它。真心喜欢一个小朋友，就送它回自己的家。
content: 宝宝呀，上一周，当当学会了让小叶子飘起来一尺高，把你逗得咯咯笑。这一周呀，八月的傍晚，常州的天边红彤彤的，晚风软软的，院子里的草丛忽然响起一个小小的声音——唧、唧、唧，细细的，抖抖的，像有谁在哭。
